#807. Miley Cyrus Marries Maxx Morando After 5 Years of Dating

Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando tied the knot in Palm Springs, Calif., on Nov. 21 after five years together.

Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando are having the ultimate party in U.S.A.

Nearly one year after the Grammy winner and Liily drummer revealed their engagement, the couple tied the knot on Nov. 21 in Palm Springs, Calif., following five years of dating, Miley confirmed on social media.

Alongside sweet black-and-white photos of the newlyweds, shot by photographer Jose Villa, the "Climb" singer wrote on Instagram Nov. 22, "M + M 11.21.26."

As for who was there to watch something beautiful happen as Miley, 33, and Maxx, 28, exchanged their vows? Well, her father Billy Ray Cyrus and his partner Elizabeth Hurley were among Miley's loved ones in attendance, as well as Elizabeth's son Damien Hurley, per photos obtained by DeuxMoi.

Meanwhile, Miley’s sisters Brandi Cyrus and Noah Cyrus as well as their mom Tish Cyrus and stepdad Dominic Purcell also witnessed the climb to the Last Song star's next chapter.

And the Hannah Montana alum wasn’t having visions of white, but was the embodiment of one as she stunned in a long-sleeved Saint Laurent by Anthony Vaccarello gown that featured a low-cut back while saying "I do." Meanwhile, the groom matched the guests in a black suit, which was also designed by Saint Laurent, according to a press release from the French fashion house.

Miley—who was previously married to Liam Hemsworth from 2018 to 2020—began dating Maxx in 2021 after they were set up on a blind date through his bandmate's sister's friend, he told Wonderland magazine in July.

As for the proposal, the couple proved that true love hit them like a wrecking ball when Maxx popped the question during a vacation in Japan, getting down on one knee in a beautiful Japanese garden.

“It was a little dead end, this beautiful Japanese forest-y situation,” Maxx told Wonderland. “She was taking videos, and was turned away. That’s when I got on one knee and tapped her on the shoulder.”

And although the “Toro” singer admitted that he was so nervous he “could feel my heart pounding,” he was able to pull off the surprise, which Miley shared wasn’t a simple feat.

“I am not easy to surprise,” she admitted during an appearance on Good Morning America following her engagement news. “I love to control every situation. I had completely surrendered. I’m telling you, I was so, so, so surprised.”

And before long, she was teasing that her and Maxx’s special day was on the horizon, releasing “Let’s Get Married” on her September 2026 album Bass Persuades, with the pair also giving an intimate glimpse into their romance in the song's music video.

“Let’s go get married tonight / Let’s get married / I’m having visions of white,” Miley sings in the track's chorus. “Let’s get married / Let’s turn the rest of our lives to a holiday / Anytime, any place, we can run away / Get married tonight / Let’s get married.”

But the couple didn't only work together on the romantic track, as Maxx additionally produced several other songs on the album.

And there’s a reason they always find their way back home to the studio, as Miley told Harper’s Bazaar in 2024, “Maxx just inspires me so much.”

But beyond their musical collaborations, the “Flowers” singer also credits Maxx with helping her with “starting over” and “building again” after she and ex Liam's California home burned down in the 2018 Malibu fires, before later separating.

“After I lost my house in the fires, that wasn't all that I lost,” Miley shared during a December press conference, per Hello! magazine. “I really actually went down to the ashes and rebuilt my life personally and physically [with] my home.”

And as Miley and Maxx enter the new chapter of their romance as newlyweds, keep reading for a look back at where their relationship began…

Miley Cyrus and musician Maxx Morando began dating in 2021. "We got put on a blind date," she recalled to British Vogue in 2023. "Well, it was blind for me and not really for him. I thought, 'The worst that can happen is I leave.'"

Miley didn't leave and, as their romance blossomed, the pair went red carpet official at the Gucci Love Parade event on November 2, 2021.

Miley and Maxx, who is a drummer in the band Liily, enjoyed a night out seeing Chicago on Broadway.

The "Flowers" singer and her boyfriend stepped out together at a Versace runway show in West Hollywood on March 9, 2023.

Maxx was by Miley's side when she won her first-ever Grammy at the 2024 award ceremony. The couple even shared a sweet smooch at their table during the event, and Miley referred to Maxx in her acceptance speech as "my love."

They returned to the Grammy Awards in 2025 for another public date night. "He’s very similar to me," Miley told Harper's Bazaar in an interview published November 2024. "We just don’t take life too seriously."

Maxx, who is six years younger than the Hannah Montana star, joined Miley on the red carpet at SNL50: The Anniversary Special, to celebrate 50 years of Saturday Night Live.

The musicians got glammed up for a big night out at the 2025 Oscars ceremony.

And later that night they stepped out in fresh looks for an appearance at the Vanity Fair Oscar Party.

It was a party in the U.S.A. when the pair got married in Plam Springs.

#806. Liverpool hand Pochettino nightmare Manchester United start after Yoro sees red

Green shoots of recovery have lasted longer in a blast furnace than in the Mauricio Pochettino era at Manchester United. On another abysmal Anfield day for the fallen giants of Manchester, Pochettino endured a baptism of fire from the eighth minute onwards when Leny Yoro was sent off for denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity. Liverpool would not be denied anything else while tormenting their old rivals yet again.

Andoni Iraola indulged in his first fist-pumps towards the Kop after an utterly dominant, comfortable win illuminated by Rio Ngumoha and Florian Wirtz brilliance plus goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Víctor Muñoz. Liverpool’s two creative forces were also on the scoresheet as Ngumoha became the youngster scorer in the fixture’s Premier League history.

“Poch is at the wheel” was the mocking, merciless soundtrack that accompanied the end of the former Tottenham, Chelsea and USA coach’s first traumatic game in the job. There may well be more. On this evidence, 19th in the Premier League is not a misleading reflection of United’s position.

The latest calamity in United’s worst start to a season for 40 years cannot be pinned on a head coach who met his new charges only on Wednesday. There can be no genuine takes on Pochettino’s vision for United either, given how quickly he was forced to turn his first game into a damage-limitation exercise. But there was one firm conclusion to be drawn. His first big call in the job proved a serious mistake with destructive repercussions for United’s entire evening.

That ill-fated decision was to hand Matthijs de Ligt a first Premier League start in 12 months at the expense of Harry Maguire. Maguire may be a symbol of United’s inertia, but his replacement at centre-back was heavily responsible for the chaos that quickly unfolded. The Netherlands international was at fault for three goals. Liverpool, under instruction from Iraola to start strong and “make them feel pressure from the beginning”, could hardly believe their luck at the first mishap in the visitors’ central defence.

• Accounting for 3pts/win all-time, Manchester United’s eight points this season are their fewest after 11 games of a league campaign since 1972-73 (7). That is also the previous season in which the Red Devils managed only one win through their first 11 league matches.

• Mauricio Pochettino (pictured) suffered the joint-heaviest defeat by a Manchester United manager in his first game (0-4), along with a defeat by the same scoreline for Lal Hilditch in October 1926 (0-4 v Bolton Wanderers in the top flight).

• Manchester United end the day in 19th position in the Premier League, with this the first time since November 1986 that they have been within the bottom two places of the league table having played at least 10 matches (21st in that case).

• Mauricio Pochettino was the first manager in Premier League history to see his team concede twice and receive a red card in the first half of his first match in charge of a club. Opta

De Ligt lost the flight of the ball and his man, Isak, when Ronald Araújo pinged a routine pass down Liverpool’s right-hand channel. Isak was suddenly away, De Ligt all at sea, and to compound matters Yoro was slow to react to the danger. By the time United’s covering defender was across to challenge Isak it was too late. Yoro clattered into the back of the Sweden international just outside the area and was shown a straight red card by the referee, Sam Barrott. Isak’s heavy first touch could not save Yoro. The free-kick could not save United from double jeopardy. Szoboszlai swept a powerful set piece into Senne Lammens’ bottom right-hand corner from 19 yards.

Pochettino claimed the dismissal was wrong and United should have had a penalty moments earlier for a Jérémy Jacquet challenge on Bryan Mbeumo. It was a desperate take. A simple detail showed the extent of the job United’s latest head coach has on his hands: the wall that lined up to face Szoboszlai’s free-kick. Just getting that right was beyond this group of players. White shirts lined up to protect the left side of Lammens’ goal but, with the isolated exception of Bruno Fernandes, no one covered the spot where the ball was ultimately placed.

Liverpool devoured the gifts. When the hosts doubled their lead three minutes later thoughts of another 7-0 humiliation for United did not seem unreasonable. Ngumoha tormented Diogo Dalot from the first whistle, as everyone inside the ground expected he would. Having been found by Isak’s cross-field pass the teenager breezed past Dalot to the byline and lifted a cross slightly behind Wirtz. The German playmaker, left in space by De Ligt, improvised brilliantly to hook a volley into the roof of the net while floating in mid-air. United were sinking into the abyss.

The first chants of “sacked in the morning” flowed from the Kop towards a disbelieving United head coach. There were 14 minutes on the clock. It was, of course, a ludicrous chant. It might be months before United’s hapless owners are seeking another scapegoat.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Pochettino responded in the only way he could to the onslaught and introduced Maguire into a rejigged five-man defence. Whether in the knowledge that United possessed neither the ability nor the inclination to hurt them, Liverpool eased off for the remainder of the first half although Isak and Alexis Mac Allister could have extended the lead.

• Since the start of the 2021-22 season, Liverpool's four wins by 4+ goals against Manchester United are the most any Premier League team has achieved against another across all competitions.

• Andoni Iraola is unbeaten in his seven Premier League matches against Manchester United (W3 D4). The only manager to record a longer unbeaten run against the Red Devils in the competition is Jürgen Klopp (8 between 2018 and 2022).

• This was the quickest Liverpool had gone 2-0 up in a Premier League match against Manchester United, going two ahead after just 12 minutes and 40 seconds.

• Rio Ngumoha (18y 85d) became the youngest player to score and assist in a Premier League game for Liverpool since Michael Owen on Boxing Day 1997 (18y 12d v Leeds United).

• Dominik Szoboszlai (pictured) scored his fifth direct free kick for Liverpool in the Premier League; only Jamie Redknapp (8), Steven Gerrard (7) and Trent Alexander-Arnold (6) have netted more for the club in the competition.

• Florian Wirtz created 10 chances in open play for Liverpool, the most by a player in a Premier League match since Manchester City’s David Silva against West Brom in March 2015 (11). Opta

Liverpool did not let their rivals off so lightly after the restart. Bradley Barcola could and should have provided Wirtz with a hat-trick of assists but squandered three beautiful touches from his fellow £100m+ recruit. Virgil van Dijk put a free header wide from another fine delivery by Wirtz. Barcola turned provider in devastating style, however, to create the goal Ngumoha’s display richly deserved. The France winger burst away from Lisandro Martínez and Fernandes with one flick of the ball before delivering an assist on a plate for the teenager to convert.

Iraola’s thoughts started to drift towards the midweek Champions League trip to Club Brugge and he started resting players from the 72nd minute onwards. But Liverpool were not done. Another mistake by De Ligt, this time a sloppy pass infield, was pounced on by Wirtz who released Muñoz inside the box. The Liverpool substitute stroked an emphatic finish past Lammens. All Sir Alex Ferguson could do up in the directors’ box in the closing stages was laugh with his friend the actor James Nesbit. The alternative is too bleak for a proud United man to contemplate.

#804. Champion’s corner: KC Current win first NWSL Championship with 2-1 stunner over Spirit

Current’s opener came direct from a corner kick

Debinha, Trinity Rodman trade goals in stoppage time

Washington Spirit lose third consecutive NWSL final

Read Jeff Rueter’s minute-by-minute report

It took five years, 90 minutes and a goal for the ages, but the Kansas City Current have their first-ever NWSL championship.

Riding a wave of momentum created by a 54th-minute Olimpico from midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo, and capping it off with an all-important breakaway winner from Debinha, the Current silenced the partisan, sellout crowd at the heavily-favored Washington Spirit’s home ground with a 2-1 victory on Saturday.

The Spirit, heartbroken at the final whistle, have now lost three consecutive NWSL Championships.

“Obviously this one hurts way worse than any of the other ones,” forward Trinity Rodman said afterward. “I don’t even think you have words in this moment — it is too fresh.”

DiBernardo’s goal was stunning, a driven, bent corner kick played to the far post that eluded Spirit goalkeeper Sandy MacIver, her defenders and Current forward Haley Hopkins, potentially DiBernardo’s intended target. The Spirit’s players and fans alike pleaded with center referee Joshua Encarnación, suggesting he examine the play on VAR for obstruction, as MacIver had potentially been screened. The review never came.

Whether played directly on goal intentionally or otherwise, the effort will go down as one of the most memorable in NWSL Championship history. At 34, DiBernardo becomes the oldest player in league history to score in a final, and was later named the match’s MVP.

“I’ve been to the game a few times and haven’t won, but this one just felt a little lighter,” said DiBernardo, who gave birth to Charlie, her first child, in January and took time off before returning to the Current in March. “I think just having Charlie, it just brings a different perspective on life. I knew the game was big and it was a big moment, but just kinda having her, just spending the day with her, it just felt really special.”

The game’s early phases were forgettable save for one incident which would go on to affect the remainder of the match: a bruising, high-speed tackle on Rodman by Current defender Laney Rouse in the fifth minute. The challenge sent Rodman flying and appeared to injure her left elbow; the Spirit forward, nearing tears, spent much of the first half in visible pain and seemingly never fully recovered. Rouse was not cautioned for the challenge.

“[It helped set the tone] in the sense that it hurt really bad, yes,” Rodman said. “As a team, you always want to put the first hit in. You’re taught to do that. Credit to them. I wish I was the one who put her on the ground. They did a really good job at setting the tone and controlling the first half.”

It was far from the game’s only physical moment. Neither team managed to settle into any meaningful rhythm during an opening 45 that felt at times more like a title fight than a title match. Encarnación, involved in his first NWSL final, called a very tight match and the near-constant stoppages in play were the defining characteristic of a sometimes ugly opening phase. In many ways it was not entirely his fault: the message-sending start from KC and the Spirit’s subsequent response often compelled him to act. The 19 combined first-half fouls between both sides were the most in any half of any NWSL title match in league history.

“It felt like we couldn’t play more than two minutes without a whistle,” Rodman said. “We were fouling, they were true calls for sure — but I think you lose control of the game really quickly that way ... It definitely messed with our rhythm a little bit.”

Paradoxically, though, the match was won with speed. Deep into second-half stoppage time, the Current found their eventual match-winner on a breakaway. After doggedly winning back possession after a Spirit free kick late on, Kansas City forward Debinha streaked upfield from just beyond the center stripe, looking off a wide-open Temwa Chawinga and rounding MacIver who looked on hopelessly as the Brazilian slotted it home.

No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football

Moments later, Rodman – somehow still in the match after not only the early challenge but a later high-speed collision with Current goalkeeper Lorena – pulled one back for the Spirit. Falling away from goal 10 yards out, Rodman got her head on the end of a Tara Rudd cross, placing it perfectly over Lorena’s outstretched arms and into the far-side netting. The ensuing five minutes – the game ended in the 102nd – were chaotic but the Spirit couldn’t quite find the equalizer.

After a slow start, the Current were well-managed by former Major League Soccer and US national team member Chris Armas. Armas was widely considered a controversial selection at the time of his appointment but proceeded to lead the club to their first championship in his first season, doing so by beating Gotham FC and now the Spirit, two sides picked by many as potential league-winners.

“I think from the front to the back we made it a point that every person on this team defends and if somebody is going to make a mistake the other person is going to have their back,” Current defender Izzy Rodriguez said. “We try and turn every 1v1 situation into a 1v2 for us, and I think that showed up today. We were winning our duels and second balls and those are things that win games.”

For the Spirit, the loss is devastating. They become the first American professional club – men’s or women’s – to lose three consecutive finals since the New England Revolution of Major League Soccer, who did so in the mid 2000s. In their five Championship appearances, the Spirit have won just one time, in 2021.

#803. 'Rolls-Royce' Iqbal's 'dream' journey from Old Trafford to Tannadice

Jim Goodwin's side are eight games unbeaten, with Zidane Iqbal pivotal

Given the superlatives being thrown in the direction of Zidane Iqbal by the Scottish football fraternity, one would think he was a replica of a certain France great instead of just sharing his name.

So much so that BBC Radio Scotland pundits were suggesting on Saturday's Sportsound that the 23-year-old is the answer to Celtic's hunt for a long-term successor to captain Callum McGregor as their midfield general.

It is just as well for Dundee United that the Iraq international is tied to them until at least the summer, his early season appearances for Utrecht ruling out a transfer during the January window.

So, where has he sprung from and what is all the fuss about?

Hibs 0-4 Dundee United: What Goodwin said

Born in Manchester to a Pakistani father and an Iraqi mother, Iqbal came through the Old Trafford youth system.

He signed his first professional contract with United in 2021 and became the first British-born South Asian and first-ever British South Asian to play in the Champions League when he came on as an 89th-minute substitute against Young Boys that December.

However, that was to be his one and only first-team appearance and, although he had already made his international debut in a World Cup qualifier at the age of 19, he was sold to Utrecht for a reported fee of Â£1m in summer 2023.

Starting off in their Jong Utrecht second string, he would go on to make 49 appearances for the Dutch top-flight outfit before making a surprise switch to the Scottish Premiership this summer.

On the one hand, United were getting a player who played all three of Iraq's games at this summer's World Cup, two of them starts, albeit all three were heavy defeats.

On the other hand, Iqbal had only managed seven appearances last season for Utrecht and had been a second-half substitute in two of their four matches at the start of the new campaign.

However, after a pivotal display in what was being described as a midfield "masterclass" by United in Saturday's 4-0 dismantling of hosts Hibernian, manager Jim Goodwin revealed he always had belief the Tangerines were unearthing a "Rolls-Royce".

"The head of recruitment's job is to go and identify good talent for us," Goodwin told BBC Scotland. "It's my job to give him the profile and then he goes out and does the groundwork.

"We could see immediately when we watched the footage of Zidane and when we had the Zoom call with him and his representatives, we not only had a fantastic player but a really good person with the right characteristics to come and fit the culture here."

Zidane Iqbal was also a marked man at the World Cup finals

While on-loan Rangers man Lyall Cameron was among the goals and fellow 24-year-old Dylan Tait provided a stylish assist, it was the third leg of what some regard as the best midfield triumvirate in the Premiership who was singled out for most praise at Easter Road.

With former Celtic winger Aidan McGeady again pondering the question about McGregor's likely successor, transfer market expert and former United wing-back Allan Preston opined: "A six for Celtic? Look no further than young Iqbal.

"He's been magnificent since he's come to Scottish football, absolutely brilliant. Running the show again.

"If Celtic are looking for a young boy at his age with experience, he is a full international, knows the game, played in Scotland, you can see what he can do, there's your man in front of you.

"Other players' hair's on fire, but he's just nice and calm. He's at a different level. He doesn't panic. When the ball comes to him, he is so calm on it, he takes his time, he's got great peripheral vision."

The former Dundee United wing-back pointed out, though: "He's had his two clubs that he can play for in a year of football, so he is going nowhere until at least the summer, so enjoy him while you can because I think you'll get serious money for this young boy."

McGeady pointed to Iqbal's "good pedigree", having started with Manchester United and already having 32 caps for Iraq, but wondered if that would be enough for Celtic to consider him.

"I don't even think, if he's performing this well, Celtic will go and get him," said McGeady.

"Why are Celtic not looking at players like this? Do they feel they have to prove themselves somewhere else first?"

Former Celtic captain Scott Brown was similarly impressed.

"He's been a delight to watch - sharpness to get on the ball and willingness to drive forward," the former midfielder and manager pointed out.

"He beats a man in the middle of the park as well and there's not too many midfielders willing to do that.

"Watching him there talking to the media, he can't get the smile off his face. He enjoys football, he takes the ball under pressure, he does things that other people don't do, especially in midfield.

"He brings composure, but he can also drive through as well. His willingness to keep getting on the ball, even if he makes that slight mistake - that's what I really enjoy watching about him."

While Goodwin reckons there will be likely interest in the summer, Iqbal has no thoughts of so quickly leaving a club - and manager - who have resurrected his club career.

"I'm not even looking at any other clubs," he told BBC Scotland. "I'm fully focused on Dundee United.

"They've given me a platform to enjoy myself and play football. I'm really enjoying my football again.

"They've given me faith and confidence. The gaffer and the coaching staff have a lot of belief in me.

"The bare minimum I can do is pay them back with strong performances and hopefully it carries on."

Iqbal recalled being at Manchester United's "development centre since I was four or five - I signed when I was eight", explaining that he "then left for some first-team football".

He stressed that his lack of games last season came as a result of "a couple of injuries" and, while "I learnt a lot in Holland", he is "happy to have left that behind me", adding: "That book's closed now."

Visit our Dundee United page for all the latest news, analysis and fan views

Get Dundee United news notifications in the BBC Sport app

Iqbal also recalled how Goodwin's enthusiasm persuaded him to make the switch to Tannadice on deadline day.

"After the World Cup, I had one year left on my contract and I was in touch with my agent," the midfielder said. "We both wanted a move and I had a few chats with a few clubs.

"To be fair, I left it a bit late for Dundee United, but after the first call with the gaffer, I straight away called my agent after we ended the call.

"I said, 'look, I genuinely feel like the guy really believes in me'.

"It happened very late. I had to drive from Holland to Scotland. It was a tough drive but worth it in the end."

That World Cup was also a defining experience, with representing his country in the United States described as surreal.

"Having your friends and family there to watch you and playing on the world stage, with so many people, was a dream," he said.

"Playing against top players gave me that confidence boost I needed. I thought I did well in the three tough games.

"I knew, wherever I'd end up, with the faith of the gaffer, I could really kick on and push because I've learnt so much from the World Cup."

Goodwin is the manager to have done that and Iqbal added: "He's such a top guy, not just in football.

"His tactics are amazing. Everyone's comfortable. Everyone wants to fight for him."

#802. ‘Obviously it’s not good’: Arteta sweating over David Raya’s fitness after injury

Keeper close to tears at Newcastle after hurting shoulder

Arsenal held 2-2, with Jaissle hailing ‘excellent’ display

Arsenal were left sweating on the fitness of their goalkeeper David Raya after the Spaniard was forced off with a shoulder injury during the second half of the 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday evening.

It left Mikel Arteta’s side six points clear of Brighton and Manchester City at the top of the Premier League but Arsenal’s manager was more concerned about Raya following an accidental collision with Newcastle’s William Osula. The Spaniard was helped off in evident pain and looked close to tears.

“Obviously it’s not good David had to come off but at the moment I don’t know [the prognosis],” said Arteta, explaining that a keeper who kept seven clean sheets in the season’s opening 10 games will have the joint scanned on Sunday. “He will have an MRI tomorrow. We will have more information tomorrow. But we know how important David is to us.”

Arsenal were 1-0 up at half-time at St James’ Park thanks to a goal from Eberechi Eze during an opening 45 minutes dominated by the visitors. Newcastle, though, improved significantly after the break and took the lead thanks to goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw before Noni Madueke equalised.

In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.

“My feeling is we have lost two points,” said Arteta. “We were exceptional in the first half but we needed to score three or four goals and we didn’t. We knew there’d be a response but the way we gave Newcastle’s first goal away was completely unacceptable. We came back and scored a second goal but we lacked the moment of magic to kill the game. I don’t think we switched off in the second half; sometimes you have to praise the opposition.”

Matthias Jaissle was left smiling after that second-half performance rescued a game watched by Newcastle’s chair, Yasir al-Rumayyan. He had flown in from Riyadh to witness his first match of the season and is believed to have complimented his head coach afterwards.

“What you saw in the second half was Newcastle’s DNA par excellence and that’s something we can build on,” said Jaissle. “But we’ve got to be humble and realistic. The first half was not good and the second half was excellent. I’ve got mixed feelings because a little more was possible but a point was probably fair.

“I was a bit frustrated at half-time but we encouraged the players to do the high press in the right way and adopt a front-foot approach. There was no hesitating, no doubting, just pure belief and we clicked. I knew we were able to do it, so I was really pleased. We felt unbelievable connections and synergy with the crowd.

“To get a team as good as Arsenal shaking in your stadium was unbelievable. I hope we can carry on this feeling.”

#801. Pepe did not injure eyes staring at sun, say Villarreal

Nicolas Pepe (right) wore an eye mask on his return to the side following his eye operation in October

Villarreal say reports striker Nicolas Pepe needed eye surgery because he stared directly at the solar eclipse are "completely false".

In a statement, the Spanish club said an operation in October that ruled the 31-year-old out for six matches was "scheduled in advance" and "entirely unrelated" to the eclipse, which took place on 12 August.

Reports on social media suggested the former Arsenal forward had injured his eyes staring directly at the sun during the lunar event, with a video then emerging - purportedly from one of Pepe's social media accounts - showing him watching it in Spain.

"Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe's eye surgery has any connection to viewing the solar eclipse," said the club.

"The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event.

"The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players' health."

Staring at an eclipse without protection can damage the retina, which sits at the back of the eye, and particularly those cells responsible for sharp central vision.

In the build-up to this summer's event, experts warned only genuine specially-designed solar eclipse glasses should be used, and that ordinary sunglasses or other devices were not enough to prevent potential damage.

Pepe has scored 14 goals in 86 appearances in all competitions for Villarreal after joining from Trabzonspor in 2024.

He cost Arsenal a then-club record Â£72m when he joined from Lille in the summer of 2019.

Pepe scored 27 goals in 112 games for the Gunners and had a loan spell at Nice before joining Trabzonspor on a free transfer.

#800. Miley Cyrus' Romance With Husband Maxx Morando Is Something Beautiful

These days Miley Cyrus is painting her nails cherry read to match her diamond from husband Maxx Morando. As the couple of five years celebrate their wedding, look back at how their love bloomed.

Sure, Miley Cyrus can buy her own flowers, write her name in the sand.

But it's hard to argue that anyone can love the three-time Grammy winner better than her newly minted husband Maxx Morando can.

Just under a year after they got engaged, the pair officially said "I do" Nov. 21, according to Entertainment Tonight.

And before the Hannah Montana alum and Liily drummer walked down the aisle, they made sure their guests had the best of both worlds. The couple kicked off the weekend with a rehearsal dinner that was certainly a party in the U.S.A. serving up filet mignon and Maine lobster ravioli.

And let's not forget the dessert spread, featuring chocolate caramel layer cake, vanilla crème brûlée and raspberry sorbet. Each treat even came with an “M+M” design in honor of the newlyweds.

While the menu was sweet, Cyrus' feelings for Morando are even sweeter.

"We've been together six years, and I've never gotten the ick," she told Zane Lowe in an interview shared by Apple Music Sept. 17. "All of a sudden I got in my head, I was like, ‘Oh my God, we’re about to get married. What if I get the ick?'"

"I asked him, 'What happens if you get the ick once you’re married?'" she continued. "He’s like, 'You deal with it and you move on and you don’t be a baby. The ick is for when you’re in fifth grade.'"

"I think that’s the thing that maybe generations prior didn’t teach us," Cyrus said, "that marriage doesn’t need to be a prison. It can actually be a playground."

Having watched her union with Liam Hemsworth metaphorically burn after their Malibu home went up in flames in 2018, Cyrus was good with being alone. She was gold, actually.

But when a friend floated the idea of setting her up with 28-year-old Morando on a blind date, she reflected to British Vogue in 2023, "I thought, 'The worst that can happen is I leave.'"

Instead, she found the kinda dream that can't be sold.

Mostly because, this time around, she was looking for more than just a piercing stare and effortless curls.

In the past, she acknowledged in a joint sit down with Tish Cyrus and sisters Brandi Cyrus and Noah Cyrus, her mother had encouraged her to stay "with the wrong guy," she explained to New York magazine's The Cut, "'cause they're hot.'"

Though, make no mistake, she insisted of Morando, "My man's hot as hell too. But my man also respects me."

With the rocker, she continued, "I ended up with a person who means a lot to me and treats me really well and respects me."

And that's just a few of the far more than seven things she likes about her spouse.

With his birthday mere days before hers, "he’s a Scorpio and so is his grandfather," Cyrus raved during a June 2025 appearance on the Sorry We're Cyrus podcast, "that’s what makes Maxx just so cool because he can sting."

The "Can't Be Tamed" musician admittedly can get a bit crazy, so she "couldn't be with" someone that doesn't have that edge, she noted. "They would have been toast already."

But not long after she and Morando turned up at Gucci's Love Parade fashion show together in November 2021, it became clear they had the right recipe.

"We just don't take life too seriously," she told Harper's Bazaar in 2024, describing her frequent collaborator as "very similar" to herself. Decades into her career, she continued, she had a pattern of working "with the people that I love. And Maxx just inspires me so much."

As the pair embark on something beautiful, take a look back at their journey so far.

#799. Robins ‘aims for the stars’ as Stoke dream of Premier League return

The Championship’s form side climbed to second after holding on resiliently with 10 men to knock Birmingham off the summit

There have been false dawns before. Plenty of them. This time last year, with Christmas on the near horizon, Stoke sat second in the Championship table and were beginning to wonder whether they might allow themselves to dream. So hopeless was their subsequent run that by the onset of spring they were forced to consider a potential relegation fight.

Experience has taught the benefit of pragmatism, so no one will be getting ahead of themselves just yet. But this weekend was supposed to be the big test for Mark Robins’s team and few considered they would pass it quite so resoundingly.

Facing a Birmingham side who arrived top of the table and with firmly held Premier League ambitions, Stoke dominated for an hour, the hitherto goal-shy George Hirst earning a well-deserved lead to send a bumper crowd into raptures. The hand-wringing that then followed Luca Bombino’s sending-off with half an hour remaining made the victory that followed all the sweeter. The 10 men of Stoke were superb. It was no surprise that it took considerable time to convince those in the stands to depart for home after the final whistle.

You see, it is not just that Stoke are second in the table, kept off top spot by goal difference. It is not even that they are undoubtedly the Championship’s form side, with just one defeat in their past 13 games. It is the whole feeling around the place; the resilience Robins has developed, and the belief that they can take on the big guns and beat them.

“We are a work in progress, but today was that step in quality against different opponents. A step up in class,” said Robins. “I thought we were really, really good. The intensity, bravery and the intent that we showed was everything that we asked for.

“And, on the back of that, you’ve got the support that are absolutely right behind us. They trust the players. That is a really good feeling. It’s a great feeling for the players. It’s a heady mix, really.”

Eight years have passed since Stoke were last in the top flight; eight years spent as the Championship equivalent of a sea sponge, doing the bare minimum to survive and letting defeats wash over them while remaining resolutely attached to the rocks of the bottom half of the table. During that time they have ended every campaign no higher than 14th and no lower than 18th. Now, something altogether different is afoot. And this may well be the win that convinces supporters to trust their upbeat instincts.

There was an unavoidable fact heading into Saturday’s game. Stoke’s four defeats this season had all come when tasked with opponents fighting at the top end of the table in Swansea, Southampton, Wolves and Middlesbrough. They had shown themselves capable against much of the division, but a failure to deliver against another Championship heavyweight would have raised legitimate questions about their realistic aspirations.

The three August defeats at the start of the campaign preceded the departure of their best player, Sorba Thomas. His replacement, Jack McGlynn, has been an inspired signing. That this victory came without the talismanic figure of Ethan Galbraith, who was absent through illness, is considerable.

As well as switching to a three-man defence following those season-opening losses, a key factor in their upturn has been the restoration of a touch of old-school Stoke; a physicality that was frequently evident on a cold Saturday afternoon.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Bobby Madley, the referee, did not always take kindly to such an approach – to the indignation of the home crowd, who frequently made their feelings clear – but there was no complaint over Bombino’s sending-off for a second yellow after a rash challenge that left him head in hands before the card had even been shown. Tears followed on his slow trudge towards the tunnel, but he need not have worried, with Birmingham barely threatening thereafter.

Given just five points separate the top eight in the Championship table, it would come as no great shock to see Stoke drop off at some point. They do not have the financial benefit of recent Premier League parachute payments or big-spending owners, they are not prolific goalscorers, and a look at their expected goals and expected points tallies shows them firmly in the bottom half of the table. But they are finding ways to win and if McGlynn has a habit of scoring from unexpectedly long distances, perhaps it is because he is good at it.

Before this weekend, Robins had revealed that a top-eight finish was the pre-season target. “You aim for the stars and hopefully you land trying to grab hold of one,” he had said, rather poetically.

If promotion is a “P” they dare not yet speak of, another one – playoffs – is becoming an increasingly realistic proposition. No more sticking to a rock. Swim free and prosper.

#798. Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

The Riemann hypothesis has been a lodestar for generations of mathetmaticians. Credit: James Brittain/Getty

In a year that has seen artificial intelligence reach one spectacular mathematical breakthrough after another, Anthropic has now claimed the top prize of them all: a full proof of the Riemann hypothesis, the statement that many mathematicians consider the most important open problem in the field. But on the same day as the Anthropic claim, a separate study claiming to have proven the Riemann also emerged — and this one is entirely human written.

The Anthropic announcement came on 20 November from Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at the San Francisco, California company. “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge wrote, referring to Anthropic’s large language model (LLM).

“If this fully checks out, it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics,” says number theorist James Maynard, a Fields Medal winner at the University of Oxford, UK, says.

Anthropic AI ‘formalizes’ proof of Fermat’s last theorem — a milestone for mathematics

Anthropic AI ‘formalizes’ proof of Fermat’s last theorem — a milestone for mathematics

Hours later, Ravi Vakil, a mathematician at Stanford University in California, posted online a rival preprint to Alpöge’s, in what Vakil called a “hurried announcement.” The preprint was written by Alessandro Maria Masullo, a mathematician who received his PhD at Stanford in 2020 under the supervision of number theorist Brian Conrad. “The hope was to have Brian work with Alessandro for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after running it by enough people,” Vakil wrote. “Now it seems best to put out the current draft.”

The confirmation of either or both solutions would be a spectacular bicentenary present for Bernhard Riemann, the German mathematician who was born 200 years ago this September and who formulated the problem, which addresses the distribution of prime numbers, in the mid-1800.

The Riemann hypothesis is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which has its scientific headquarters in Oxford, UK , at the turn of the twenty-first century. The institute offers a US$1 million prize to anyone who devises a solution to one of the problems, which are considered some of the most challenging in the field. Mathematicians using AI tools announced earlier this year that they had solved another Millennium problem, related to the Navier-Stokes equation.

The problem has to do with the ‘Riemann ζ function’ (ζ is the Greek letter zeta), which encodes the randomness properties of the prime numbers. Riemann discovered that the distribution of primes is encoded in the ζ function’s ‘zeroes.’ These are points, denoted by z, on a plane satisfying the equation ζ(z) = 0.

Riemann conjectured that apart from some obvious but uninteresting cases, all such solutions had to lie on a certain vertical line in the plane. If this were true, he showed, it would imply that prime numbers are scattered among all whole numbers in a way that is essentially as random as it could be.

Alpöge’s 4-page document includes a sketch of the proof. But Andrew Granville, a number theorist at the University of Montreal in Canada, says that Alpöge should have taken the time to prepare a clearer write-up before making the announcement, which came just days after Anthropic’s initial public offering (IPO). The IPO initially valued the company at US$1.5 trillion, but the company’s valuation dropped on 19 November.

“What he released is garbled,” Granville says of Alpöge’s document. Granville cites the downturn in the company’s stock value as the reason for the timing of the proof’s release.

“There is an obvious cynical view, to do with the timing, but it is false,” Alpöge wrote in the document.

Anthropic did not respond immediately to Nature’s request for comment.

Tristan Buckmaster, a mathematician at New York University who collaborated with Alpöge on a separate project regarding the Navier-Stokes equation, says that Alpöge deserves a lot of credit for developing techniques to produce mathematical results using LLMs. “Levent himself built this amazing setup to do math”. He adds that Alpöge, who is himself a number theorist on leave from Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has been working relentlessly for months on this and other problems, hardly ever getting any sleep.

‘The job description is changing’: mathematician Terence Tao on the rise of AI

‘The job description is changing’: mathematician Terence Tao on the rise of AI

“I suspect that the proof will turn out to be correct,” Maynard says of the Alpöge announcement, even though it is now in the form of incomprehensible code in the Lean programming language.

“At the moment, it apparently is crazily complicated. It’s going to take a long time for mathematicians to digest,” says Buckmaster. Maynard agrees, but he adds, “assuming we do get the corresponding understanding, this will surely be viewed as one of the absolute pinnacles of mathematical results”.

#796. Blackburn earn derby draw for Mowbray and extend Burnley’s wait for home win

Todd Cantwell’s penalty earned Blackburn a 2-2 draw at Burnley in their first match since Tony Mowbray stepped back because of health issues.

In a gripping, physical East Lancashire derby, the home side led twice, through Largie Ramazani’s rising first-half drive and Jaydon Banel’s steered finish after the break. But Andri Gudjohnsen scored Blackburn’s first equaliser, then earned the penalty which Cantwell converted.

Burnley remain deep in relegation trouble, without a home league victory for 400 days, having once again failed to hold on to a lead. They have now dropped 25 points from winning positions in the Championship this season.

Blackburn wanted a victory not just for local pride, but to honour Mowbray, who turned 63 on Sunday, and for whom this was to be a 900th match in management before his announcement on Tuesday that he would be stepping back. Their players warmed up in T-shirts bearing the message “We’re with you, Tony” on the back and the number 900 on the front.

Coaches Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds have taken charge in Mowbray’s absence and had to reshuffle the defence when Tom Atcheson was concussed after receiving a boot to the face in the third minute.

The stand-in goalkeeper Aynsley Pears, playing after Balazs Toth sustained a broken hand on international duty with Hungary, pushed over a fierce deflected shot from Banel, but was at fault when Ramazani gave Burnley a 27th-minute lead.

The on-loan Leeds winger cut in from the right and fired a shot that flew into the roof of the net right by Pears, who was too slow to react.

But Gudjohnsen equalised four minutes later, racing on to a Harry Pickering long ball that drifted over Burnley centre-back Max Alleyne, and steering a sweet shot beyond goalkeeper Max Weiss for his 12th goal of the season. The Icelander celebrated by grabbing a Mowbray-tribute T-shirt from a photographer and displaying it for the cameras.

Blackburn finished the first half strongly, with Cantwell firing over a good chance, before Banel restored Burnley’s lead six minutes into the second half, running unchallenged to place a shot into the far corner as Hayden Carter backed off.

The home side were fortunate to escape a strong penalty appeal just before the hour mark as Cantwell burst into the penalty area and saw two attempted crosses both strike the arm of Igor Julio.

Blackburn did get a penalty with 16 minutes left as Josh Laurent, attempting to clear a low cross, failed to spot Gudjohnsen darting in from behind him and caught the striker’s leg. Cantwell drove the penalty straight down the middle to make it 2-2.

Gudjohnsen thought he had given Blackburn the lead two minutes later, when he controlled and drove a low shot against the base of the post with Weiss a spectator, but neither side could find a winner.

"Did someone say they missed king kylie," Kylie teased in the caption of her June 8 Instagram post, to which her sister Khloe Kardashian cheekily replied, "I did! I did!!!!!!"

The former Bravo star debuted a platinum blonde look during 2024 Paris Fashion Week Haute Couture.

The Heads of State star debuted a drastic haircut—a shoulder-grazing bob—while attending a Bulgari event in Rome i May 2024.

In May 2024, the actress chopped her hair into a bob that many fans on social media said reminded them of one of the looks she sported as Mary Camden on the '90s series 7th Heaven.

The Transformers actress returned to her dark brown tresses and debuted a sassy bob in May 2024, a month after she dyed her hair blue to enter what she dubbed her "Jedi era."

#794. PSG's Doue to have surgery on ruptured ACL

Desire Doue has scored six goals in all competitions for PSG this season

Paris St-Germain forward Desire Doue will have surgery later this month after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee.

The 21-year-old was in tears as he was taken off on a stretcher towards the end of the first half in the Ligue 1 champions' 3-2 victory over Nice on Saturday night.

Doue, who has arguably been PSG's best player this season, twisted awkwardly and went down under no contact.

The match was stopped for five minutes as Doue - who was visibly in pain - received treatment before he was applauded off by the crowd at the Allianz Riviera Stadium.

It is a huge set-back for the France attacker, who missed 13 games in 2025-26 with calf and hamstring injuries.

The European champions have been plagued with injury issues so far this season and are already without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who sustained an ACL injury of his own against Barcelona in October.

PSG return to action on Wednesday, when they host Roma in the Champions League.

#793. McBurnie’s added-time double snatches win for Hull to shock 10-man Brighton

Amid the talk of Brighton being surprise title contenders this season, these are perhaps the afternoons which show the margin that still exists, and how the Premier League can provide the most punishing of wake-up calls at any moment.

Make no mistake about it, Fabian Hürzeler’s side will play far worse than this over the next few months and win. They are still second in the table. How they left Hull without even a point almost defies belief given the dominance they enjoyed for large parts of the contest. But for all the statement victories and the headline-grabbing moments, these games are the ones which can trip you up the most.

A blisteringly cold November afternoon in Hull, against a promoted side where the expectation for a team challenging for the title is to win, and perhaps win with minimum fuss, too. On another afternoon, Brighton may have done just that, were it not for the heroics of Hull’s goalkeeper, Konstantinos Tzolakis.

But the best teams, the ones that end the seasons lifting the silverware, almost always seem to find a way. Tzolakis was the Seagulls’ scourge with a string of sensational saves that kept Hull in a contest where, for large periods, they were struggling to keep their heads above water.

However, the goal Brighton deserved never arrived – and as this game wore on you wondered if a team like Hull, whose commitment can never be questioned and who are tough to beat on their own turf, could dig in for long enough to provide a sucker punch on the counter. That moment arrived, not perhaps with Oli McBurnie’s goal that broke the deadlock in stoppage time, but two minutes before.

When João Costinha was shown a second yellow card in the 89th minute for a foul on Sorba Thomas, the MKM Stadium responded. They sensed that Tzolakis’s heroics could perhaps produce more than just a point, with Brighton forced to sit in and try to hold out for the closing moments. Hull surged forward, with McBurnie bundling home from close to range to spark delirium among the home support.

Two minutes later, with Brighton now left pressing just to try to find an equaliser, Hull caught them cold and McBurnie would tap into an empty net to seal the most unlikely of victories for the Tigers, who remain unbeaten at home since promotion. This was their first win since August, however, and a welcome tonic to put breathing space between themselves and the bottom three.

“We played against an excellent team who play intensive football,” Hull’s manager, Sergej Jakirovic, said. “I wish this feeling would never stop because we’ve had to wait for this.” But this was an afternoon that was as much about Brighton as it was Hull.

A win here would have closed the gap to Arsenal at the top to three points. In the end, this was a huge missed opportunity, with Hürzeler understandably crestfallen post-match.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

“In the Premier League you can never expect to win,” he said. “For us, it’s very important with our identity and every game you have to lift your standards. If you drop, the Premier League is too good and it will punish you.”

McBurnie may have been the hero but there was no doubting the star man was Tzolakis. He denied Brighton on so many occasions and otherwise the game could have been over before the interval. First, he denied Diego Gómez from close range before stopping Yasin Ayari’s effort.

Two minutes later, Georginio Rutter was the next to be denied by the Greece international with another smart save before the pick of the bunch: Tzolakis made a reaction save with his foot to turn Gómez’s effort wide after Brighton cut Hull open at will again. At that stage it felt like when, not if, the visitors went ahead. Nobody told Tzolakis that.

Half-time did little to change the flow of momentum. Pascal Gross was next to be denied by Tzolakis before Gómez then shot wide from six yards out. At the other end, Hull were showing signs of coming to life, with two Mohamed Belloumi breaks a warning sign of what was to follow for the visitors.

Tzolakis was finally beaten by Charalampos Kostoulas when his chipped effort beat his fellow countryman, but Regan Slater was on hand to clear off the line. Then, as time ebbed away, Costinha’s second yellow decisively swung the momentum and within two minutes, Hull scored the goal Brighton had craved.

First, McBurnie bundled home before Belloumi’s break led to him squaring for the Scotland international to tap into an empty net. Was it what Brighton deserved? Probably not. But try persuading anyone of a Hull persuasion to care about that.

#792. Yoro sees red as Ngumoha shines - Liverpool v Man Utd player ratings

Ngumoha stars as Liverpool thrash 10-man Man Utd

Mauricio Pochettino's reign as Manchester United manager got off to a dismal start as his side were beaten 4-0 by rivals Liverpool after playing 82 minutes with 10 men.

Here's how BBC Sport rated the players - and you can see how you scored them below.

Alisson Becker: Caught one cross and took a few goal-kicks. Made a good save to deny Bruno Fernandes in stoppage time. Had little else to do. 6

Ronald Araujo: Never really tested defensively. Made a few contributions going forward. 7

Jeremy Jacquet: Went shoulder to shoulder with Bryan Mbeumo in the box at 0-0, although a penalty against the French defender would have been harsh. 6

Virgil van Dijk: Organised the defence well. Also had a header well-saved at 0-0 and nodded another wide in the second half. 7

Milos Kerkez: Always keen to drive Liverpool up the pitch. Had some nice link-ups with Rio Ngumoha. 7

Dominik Szoboszlai: Fantastic driven free-kick to open the scoring. Went close a few more times with long shots and generally bossed the midfield. 8

Alexis Mac Allister: Did all the simple things right and allowed others to shine around him. Forced Senne Lammens into a top save in the first half. 7

Bradley Barcola: Missed a few chances to score his first league goal for Liverpool when through one-vs-one. Showed his electric pace to set up his side's third. 7

Florian Wirtz: Readjusted well to net Liverpool's second and assisted their fourth. Five goals in four games for club and country now and looks close to his creative best. 8

Rio Ngumoha: So direct and skilful. Scored Liverpool's third with a calm finish. Also set up their second after easily beating Diogo Dalot. Club and country have a real talent on their hands. 9

Alexander Isak: Led the line well but missed some big chances. Won the free-kick that resulted in Szoboszlai's goal and led to Leny Yoro's sending off. 6

Victor Munoz (on 72, Barcola): Good cameo and took his goal well, curling it into the far corner. 7

Trey Nyoni (on 72, Mac Allister): Looked bright. Had a shot go just over. 6

Subs not used: Chiesa, Mamardashvili, McConell, Tsimikas.

Senne Lammens: Could he have done better with the opener? Good save to deny Mac Allister and some decent stops after that. 6

Leny Yoro: Did he have to make the tackle on Isak? It was almost as though he thought about whether he should and decided the answer was yes. Given Liverpool scored from the free-kick it was a bad decision. 4

Matthijs de Ligt: First Premier League start in almost 12 months in middle of a back three turned into a nightmare with the early error that led to opening goal and Yoro red card. Struggled from that moment on. 4

Lisandro Martinez: Fully extended by Liverpool's attack. The least bad of the visitors' starting defence, but that isn't saying much. Exposed completely by Barcola for Liverpool's third. 5

Diogo Dalot: Given a torrid time by Ngumoha, which prompted Pochettino to bring on Maguire. Tries hard but it's not enough. 5

Youri Tielemans: Concerns about a midfield partnership with Mainoo emerge again. Not having the sustained impact required for a player of his experience. 4

Kobbie Mainoo: Twenty-one-year-old being asked to shoulder so much responsibility in an ailing team. New midfield recruits have not helped him. 5

Bryan Mbeumo: Couple of decent bursts came to nothing, then sacrificed after Yoro red card. Received consoling pat on the head from his new boss. 5

Bruno Fernandes: Early free-kick just wide and shot straight at Alisson. Given the carnage at Old Trafford this season, no wonder contract talks on hold. Furious at free-kick given against him when he thought he was through. 5

Patrick Dorgu: Asked to do an awful lot, initially as wing-back, then further back. Lucky Barcola fluffed his lines or his failure to keep an offside line would have been exposed. 5

Matheus Cunha: Tried to keep simmering frustration in check. Not easy in a losing side with no service. Replaced at the break. 5

Harry Maguire (on 22, Mbeumo): Couldn't have expected to be called on so soon. Went into middle of back three and immediately blocked an Isak effort to prevent a third goal. Tried hard. 5

Joshua Zirkzee (on 46, Cunha): Pre-match rumours of a rare start proved unfounded. Replaced Cunha at half-time and asked to bring a different skillset to the number nine role. More physical but not as good and lost possession too easily. 4

Mason Mount (on 65, Tielemans): Only on for a couple of minutes when attempted crossfield pass went to Liverpool player and eventually a third goal. 5

Noussair Mazraoui (on 65, Dorgu): Not really sure what he was supposed to do. Tried to push forward as United's poor control brought more pressure. 4

Subs not used: Heaton, Amad Diallo, Heaven, Lacey.

#791. European football: Barcelona roar back from two goals down to sink Villarreal

Barça prevail 3-2 despite Lamine Yamal’s missed penalty

Atalanta snatch point in thrilling 4-4 draw with Inter

Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 at home on Sunday and restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga.

Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and things got worse for Barça when winger Lamine Yamal missed a first-half penalty.

The Catalan giants fought back in style, striking three times in an 11-minute second-half spell to claim victory. Gerard Martín and Fermín López pulled Barça level before Pau Navarro’s own goal gave them victory.

Barça have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clàsico defeat by Real Madrid in October, and restored their three-point cushion over José Mourinho’s side, who had moved level with Saturday’s victory over Celta Vigo.

Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute, producing a perfect sliced effort from distance after López gave the ball away. Two minutes later, the visitors doubled their lead through another Canadian, as Oluwaseyi broke down the left flank and smashed an effort into the roof of the net.

Hansi Flick’s side should have pulled one back when Oluwaseyi felled Lamine Yamal in the area and a penalty was given after a VAR review. The teenager took it himself but dragged his spot-kick against the post and wide.

Barcelona came out invigorated for the second half and Peter Gulacsi saved López’s low effort before Martín headed home in the 57th minute from Pedri’s cross.

Four minutes later, López slammed home the second after being teed up by Lamine Yamal and the third was quick to follow. Lamine Yamal’s clever backheel pass fed Eric García, whose cross was bundled into the back of his own net by Navarro, who was later sent off for a second yellow card to complete a miserable afternoon.

Atlético Madrid stayed on the tail of Spain’s top two with a comfortable 3-0 derby win over Getafe.

Diego Simeone’s side are five points behind leaders Barcelona and two off Real Madrid. Álex Baena and Johnny Cardoso’s first-half goals, both set up by Julián Alvarez, got the job done away at the Coliseum stadium in the suburbs south of the Spanish capital.

Álex Grimaldo wrapped up the victory in stoppage time with a penalty, after Getafe’s Djene Dakonam was sent off for fouling Alexander Sørloth.

In Serie A, Atalanta rescued an extraordinary late 4-4 draw against Inter on Sunday as the champions fell three points off the title pace despite Pio Esposito’s hat-trick.

Inter looked comfortable in Bergamo when Petar Sucic’s penalty gave them a two-goal cushion in the 76th minute after Esposito’s goals, but Charles De Ketelaere’s second of the night and a stoppage-time Franck Kessié penalty salvaged a point.

It marked only the third time Inter have dropped points in the league this season, but kept Cristian Chivu’s side in third place, one point behind Roma and three adrift of leaders Lazio.

Esposito struck twice in the first half, pouncing on a deflected ball in the box to sweep home the opener before doubling Inter’s lead by heading home from a corner. Eljif Elmas quickly got one back for the hosts to keep the game alive, but Esposito took his third in composed fashion early in the second half, marking his eighth goal in five games for club and country.

De Ketelaere proved the catalyst for Atalanta’s fightback, pulling a goal back with a header and firing home a powerful finish either side of Sucic’s spot-kick.

That set up a thrilling conclusion as Atalanta chased what had seemed an unlikely point, which they claimed when a penalty was awarded for handball that Kessié calmly converted.

Juventus moved into the top six with a thumping 4-0 victory over Venezia as their recent upturn in form continued. Luciano Spalletti’s side were booed off after a goalless first half, but found four second-half strikes as their unbeaten run stretched to four games in all competitions.

Nick Woltemade sparked the game into life after coming off the bench, pouncing on a loose ball to smash home his second league goal in two games before turning provider for Teun Koopmeiners’ whipped finish. Juan Cabal headed home Juve’s third before Kolo Muani won and converted a penalty to complete the rout, with all four goals coming between the 53rd and 71st minute.

“In the first half, we gave the ball away too much,” Spalletti told Dazn. “It was crucial the players recognised something was missing … in the second half, the players were decisive and more relaxed.”

Milan returned to the top four as Gonçalo Ramos ended his goal drought in a 5-1 thrashing of Frosinone.

Ruben Amorim’s side sealed back-to-back wins for the first time in over a month to go fourth, five points behind leaders Lazio, as club record signing Ramos broke a five-match goalless streak.

Milan got off to a flying start with a Gabriele Calvani own goal and a composed Ramos strike inside 19 minutes. Amorim accused his players of “not helping Ramos” before the game after the Portugal international scored just twice in his first 11 league games following his summer move from Paris Saint-Germain.

His third was met with a loud roar from the San Siro crowd after he was teed up by Adrien Rabiot, who became the first Milan midfielder since Kaká in 2004 to notch a goal or assist in seven consecutive league games.

The visitors soon hit back through Patrizio Masini, but Milan pulled clear in the second half with some lethal counterattacking as substitutes Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse struck before Christian Pulisic’s dinked finish completed the biggest victory of the Amorim era.

Milutin Osmajic scored twice in a 2-0 win for Genoa at Sassuolo, while Bologna were held to a 1-1 draw by Udinese, who climb off the bottom of the table at Venezia’s expense.

In Ligue 1, Paris FC climbed to second place behind local rivals Paris Saint-Germain with a 4-0 home win over lowly Angers. Patrick Zabi, Luca Koleosho, Maxime Lopez and Diego Coppola all struck in the second half for Liam Rosenior’s high-flying side.

Le Mans struck five minutes into stoppage time to complete a stunning 3-2 comeback ⁠victory at Marseille to move ⁠clear of the ⁠relegation places.

Substitute ​Jean Vercruysse delivered the decisive blow to end Marseille’s run of five successive league victories.

Marseille appeared in complete control ⁠after Amine Gouiri scored for a fourth consecutive game and the Brazilian winger Igor Paixão doubled their lead during a dominant first half.

Louis Mafouta pulled one back with a powerful free-kick 20 ‌minutes from time, although he then had a penalty saved in the 78th minute. Erwan Colas equalised six minutes later before Vercruysse struck late to seal all three points.

Bayern Munich’s Jamal Musiala reportedly suffered another seizure in training this week, according to information received by an AFP subsidiary on Sunday.

Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in pre-season with the 23-year-old later revealing he had a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Last Monday’s incident was the second since he made the announcement; the player is reportedly adjusting his medication to properly treat the condition while continuing to play.

News of the incident comes as Bayern have faced criticism from footballers’ union Fifpro over what they claim is a “coordinated campaign” to pressure Musiala to renegotiate the contract he extended in 2025.

On Friday, Bayern’s supervisory board member and former chief executive Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the Germany international may need to take a pay cut if he cannot recapture his old form.

“Based on what we know, it unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he so often demonstrated,” Rummenigge said. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation … because frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable.”

#788. Manchester City’s WSL title bid hit by Spurs after Vinberg and Naz’s late double

This most unpredictable and evenly contested Women’s Super League campaign took another unexpected twist as Manchester City missed the chance to return to the top of the table as they suffered a second successive defeat, by virtue of a terrific performance from a Tottenham side who moved within three points of the European places.

The shock result came just 24 hours after City’s title rivals Chelsea had dropped points at Liverpool. It was the first time City had failed to win a home league match during Andrée Jeglertz’s 16 months in charge, let alone lose.

Nevertheless, the victory was fully deserved for Tottenham, who made Khadija “Bunny” Shaw wait to equal her teammate Vivianne Miedema’s all-time WSL goalscoring record of 97 goals.

Jeglertz described the defeat as a “wake-up call” for his team, adding: “Tottenham were a little bit more urgent than us. Each duel counts, each moment counts, each ball counts. That was something that I missed with our players, especially in the second half where we needed to score and we needed to beat them in one-versus-one situations. I missed a little bit of that urgency, which I think is the most important in a team, and if we drop a little bit in that, this league is so tight and tough and the teams are so good, you will drop points and lose games.”

Before the game, the anticipated storyline felt almost too obvious. Shaw, needing three goals to surpass Miedema, was facing a club against whom she had scored four hat-tricks, including on Tottenham’s most recent visit to this stadium in March, when she recorded the WSL’s fastest treble. Persistently their tormentor, Shaw has scored more goals against Spurs than any other player has managed against a single opponent in the competition.

When Shaw opened the scoring inside 10 minutes, everything seemed to be following the script. Jade Rose, pressing very high up the pitch for a centre-back, won the ball and played a precise low pass across to Shaw, who tucked into the bottom corner from inside the box to record her 96th WSL goal and her 16th against Tottenham.

That, however, proved to be the only effort at goal – on or off target – that City would register during the opening 45 minutes, as Tottenham impressed. Kirsty Hanson drew a good save from Ayaka Yamashita and Hanson also felt she had a very strong claim for a penalty when Carlotta Wamser appeared to foul her inside the area, but it was not long before the visitors were deservedly level as Cathinka Tandberg expertly turned home Hanson’s cross with a clinical near-post finish.

Tottenham continued to threaten after the break, although Rose scooped over the bar to spurn a huge City chance on the rebound after a Lauren Hemp free-kick had been parried by Lize Kop. Some very effective counterattacking football then deservedly won the game for Tottenham as they scored twice to stun the defending champions.

First, in the 74th minute, an exquisite Drew Spence through ball found the run of Matilda Vinberg – who was a late addition to the starting side after the withdrawal of Olivia Holdt during the warm-up because of stomach pains – and Vinberg showed her quality to turn Rose and fire past Yamashita. Vinberg turned provider five minutes later, to set up Jessica Naz for another good finish.

No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football

Martin Ho, the Tottenham head coach, hailed his team’s “outstanding” display, saying: “Every time we play a team who has been in the top three consistently, the conversation is: ‘Can you get one over the line?’ And, for the players, they need to feel what that feels like and enjoy that. Today we nullified a lot of their threats. That will give us a lot of confidence.”

Manchester City had won 12 of their 13 previous WSL games against Tottenham, and all of their past 17 WSL home games, but this defeat added a further dent to their title challenge after their loss at Stamford Bridge last weekend. Chelsea, held to a goalless draw by Liverpool on Saturday, remain two points clear.

Arsenal remain winless at home in the WSL this season after being held to another frustrating draw at the Emirates, this time by West Ham. Arsenal had 22 shots at goal but were unable to break the deadlock, as their under-pressure head coach, Renée Slegers, oversaw a sixth home league draw out of six, leaving Arsenal eight points behind the top three.

Manchester United left it late to come from behind and beat Birmingham 2-1 but Simi Awujo’s last-gasp header from a corner gave them a valuable win and extended Eva Olid’s side’s club-record unbeaten run to 14 matches in all competitions. Birmingham had led inside four minutes through Lee Geum-min’s expert volley but Elisabeth Terland’s close-range finish with 10 minutes to go and Awujo’s 94th-minute winner snatched it, moving Olid’s fourth-placed team just six points off the top.

Elsewhere, the bottom side Charlton collected their first point of the season as they drew 1-1 with Aston Villa, while Brighton moved into the top half with a 1-0 victory at Everton, courtesy of Maz Pacheco’s early own goal. Tom Garry

Jeglertz continued: “We will bounce back, I’m not worried about that. I know the qualities in this group. But it’s the good habits, the small details that matter. Those are the things that win titles – this was actually the first time that I missed that in a game and I’m pretty sure it’s not going to happen again.” With just seven points now separating the top five, his team can ill-afford for it to happen again.

#786. Pochettino’s new-manager bounce falls flat with De Ligt move a disastrous step | Jamie Jackson

Decision to pick the Dutch defender over Harry Maguire backfired as Manchester United fell apart in the Anfield bearpit

Chaotic, bewildering, and on this evidence in a relegation dogfight: welcome to the three‑ring circus that is Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino.

This ended as a 4-0 rout in favour of Liverpool, the new head coach overseeing the poorest opening result of the eight who have followed Sir Alex Ferguson since May 2013. Factor in this result coming against United’s fiercest rivals and Pochettino’s despair is complete.

He is firmly in the dock for this loss, due to a disastrous preference for Matthijs de Ligt over Harry Maguire, the hapless Dutch defender playing a leading part in three Liverpool goals.

Towards the end the Kop chirped: “You’re going down with the City.” There may be truth in the humour unless Pochettino gets hold – fast – of the rabble inherited from Michael Carrick.

Eight short minutes into a nascent tenure and a disgusted shake of his flowing locks was the greeting to the madhouse he has taken over. By then Leny Yoro had been sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak and Anfield was in bearpit mood.

Very far from ideal – and worse was to follow. Far worse. After the Frenchman departed, Dominik Szoboszlai smashed the free-kick through a nonexistent wall and beyond Senne Lammens and Liverpool were 1-0 up.

The visitors’ next act? To enter full meltdown as Diogo Dalot allowed Rio Ngumoha room to cross and Florian Wirtz hooked home, De Ligt losing his man.

Thirteen minutes in and 2–0 behind made Omar Berrada’s talk of the “buzz” of Pochettino’s entrance at United farcical and made the chief executive appear to be as much as a chump as his latest appointee, who was authoring a new head-coach plummet, not bounce.

Yoro had been forced into hauling down Isak after De Ligt lost first the ball, then the Liverpool striker. De Ligt’s inclusion was Pochettino’s headline selection move, the dropping of Maguire handing the centre-back a first league start in a year and it backfired almost immediately.

“I don’t know who played the last game – we assessed the squad from the day we arrived and we believe it’s the best team for today,” Pochettino said beforehand when quizzed about the XI he sent out.

Words to haunt him and, as De Ligt’s only other start was in United’s 4-1 humiliation at Como last month in the Champions League, questions regarding the coach’s judgment were already being posed.

By now “sacked in the morning” was the derisory cry of Kopites as Pochettino’s new project was in the damage-limitation mode of a 5-3-1 with 21 minutes played, as off went Bryan Mbeumo for Maguire.

After spells with Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the USA, Pochettino’s honours roll reads one Ligue 1 and one Coupe de France – a modest two trophies in a 17-year managerial career.

Losing a Champions League final (with Spurs) and two EFL Cup finals (Spurs and Chelsea) had characterised him, to some, as a “bridesmaid” and at half‑time his team were definitively second best, fortunate to be only two behind.

In the perpetual soap opera that is United, the buildup featured a drone filming Pochettino’s first training session, Berrada’s interview and Bruno Fernandes saying new contract talks between the captain and club were paused due to the worst league start in 40 years.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Going into the game, United’s dire form contained a solitary win in 10 league matches and eight points. Why? Because they are a rabble, lacking cohesion from goalkeeper to attack, with individuals consistently embarrassing themselves and the shirt.

It cost Carrick, culpable for this too, his job and cleared the path for Pochettino to occupy a role he has long coveted. Each new manager since Ferguson has faced a two-pronged challenge: the state of the squad and the state of the club – each related.

Those who know Pochettino say he will bring charm and warmth – useful, maybe, for man-managing a group of multimillionaires, but at the interval he needed to perform the miracle of convincing them that something, somehow, could be salvaged after a diabolical opening 45 minutes.

They were staring at defeat by an Andoni Iraola side that began 10 points and 15 places better off. Pochettino hoped to avoid this by taking off Matheus Cunha for Joshua Zirkzee for the second half but ended the non-contest ashen‑faced, with Berrada and Jason Wilcox, the director of football, appearing just as lost in the posh seats.

A main takeaway from Berrada’s interview was his conviction that “we are heading in the right direction”. When he spoke United were 18th, and by full time they were 19th, with De Ligt a glaring emblem of their disarray. When again he was marking air not Isak, the Swede saved the centre-back more blushes by spraying wide.

This had Pochettino applauding, unfathomably, when invective seemed an apt response.

Yet when Ngumoha made it 3-0 after 66 minutes there was no more faux touchline enthusiasm from a man who had promised to “create something from scratch”. As with all who have followed Ferguson, he had discovered that United’s shaky foundations make building anything sustainable a sisyphean task.

De Ligt’s loose pass led to Víctor Muñoz’s fourth, meaning the answer to whether Pochettino’s debut could have gone any worse was a resounding no.
