#785. Rob Kardashian Poses in Rare Family Photos for Daughter Dream's B-Day

Rob Kardashian posed for rare family photos at his daughter Dream Kardashian’s leopard-themed 10th birthday party, including one where he was all smiles with sister Khloe Kardashian.

Rob Kardashian is doing amazing, sweetie.

The Keeping Up With the Kardashians alum shared a rare photo posing with his and Blac Chyna’s daughter Dream Kardashian while celebrating her 10th birthday with an extravagant leopard-themed bash.

“Birthday fun yay yay,” Rob captioned a Nov. 21 Instagram post. “I love you Dreammmmmmmmmm.”

In one snap shared to the carousel of photos, the 39-year-old—donning a blue hat and black Nike shirt—was all smiles as his little girl leaned in close to pose for the camera.

And while the pic marks a rare sighting for the social media star, one common occurrence in Rob’s life is how he shows up for his daughter—and her special day was no different.

Elsewhere in his post, Dream—wearing a leopard-print top, matching shorts, Uggs and a chain around her neck—couldn’t contain her excitement as she smiled behind her elaborate leopard-print cake.

Sharing a closer look into the soirée, Rob’s sister Khloe Kardashian proved in her Nov. 21 Instagram post that keeping up with Dream’s cousins—including her and Tristan Thompson’s kids True Thompson, 8, and Tatum Thompson, 4—might have been difficult if it weren’t for the on-theme arts and crafts, sweet treats and dance party to keep the family’s little ones entertained.

In fact, Khloe—who wore a figure-hugging leopard ensemble to the event—and Rob were able to snag their own moment together as they also posed for a rare photo while sitting at an outdoor table.

But the backyard bash wouldn’t be the only way Rob made his little girl’s milestone birthday one to remember.

After all, he pulled out all the stop for her golden birthday Nov. 10, with the tween waking up to a bouquet of flowers, huge balloons that read “Happy 10th Birthday Dream” and donuts to commemorate the occasion.

"Happy golden Birthday to my Dream girl," Rob wrote on Instagram, referencing the one year when a person's age and date of birth align. "I can’t believe 10 years has gone by already goodness Lord please slow down time."

And while it’s true that the years are flying by, Rob is just grateful to rise and shine every day as Dream’s dad.

“Being your dad is the greatest gift of my life!” he added. “You make me proud every single day! I love you more than you’ll ever know!!”

#783. ‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card in Anfield humiliation

Manchester United lose 4-0 to Liverpool after early red

Argentinian suffers club’s joint-heaviest debut defeat

Mauricio Pochettino argued that Leny Yoro was wrongly sent off and that Manchester United were earlier denied a penalty against Liverpool after suffering the joint-heaviest debut defeat in the club’s history.

Liverpool’s emphatic 4-0 win ensured Pochettino equalled Lal Hilditch’s unwanted record from 1926 of losing his first United game by such a scoreline. United’s 34 goals conceded across all competitions this season are the most by any team in European football’s top five leagues.

United were reduced to 10 men after only eight minutes when Yoro was shown a straight red card for denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity. “He was clearly the last man and it was clearly a foul,” said the Liverpool head coach, Andoni Iraola.

Yet Pochettino took a fiercely opposing view, claiming Isak had waited for contact to be made after losing possession and insisting United should have had a penalty moments earlier for a Jérémy Jacquet challenge on Bryan Mbeumo. Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring from the free-kick that resulted from Yoro’s foul and Liverpool were coasting at 2-0 after only 14 minutes. United’s head coach said: “I don’t agree [it was a red-card offence] because the ball wasn’t in Isak’s control.

“Leny was running with him and when Isak saw the control wasn’t good and the ball was going to the keeper it is normal you delay, you stop running, and you wait to feel the touch and you go down. It is never a foul. But two minutes before, Jacquet and Mbeumo, how can you compare the situation?

“It is painful for me and for them but we played for more than 80 minutes at Anfield with 10 men. You can be critical of the team, but it’s a penalty for Mbeumo. We can make a mistake and we were punished. They can make a mistake and they were not punished.”

Pochettino defended his decision to give Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in 12 months despite the centre-back having a torrid time against Liverpool’s forward line. He also claimed United showed the resolve necessary to drag themselves out of relegation trouble despite being comprehensively outplayed.

“We need to accept the reality and we need to be united,” he said. “It is clear what happened.

“After eight minutes the plan was in the bin, but what I learned from my players is that they like to fight, they are committed to the team, to the club and they want to win games.

“Today was a test that for me is very positive. Even the best team in the world playing in these circumstances after eight minutes would concede four goals or even more. We are in a situation that is very complicated and difficult, but we fight, we make the effort.”

Rio Ngumoha became the youngest goalscorer in the fixture’s Premier League history and produced a scintillating display alongside the equally impressive Florian Wirtz. Iraola said of the teenager: “He is playing a lot of minutes, on the left and the right, and he is getting used to going outside or cutting inside to finish. I’m happy with the way he arrived in the box to score. The same with Flo. We want them to be more of a threat in the box.”

Iraola recreated Jürgen Klopp’s post-match celebration after the final whistle and fist-pumped the Kop. He said: “Obviously I enjoyed the moment. I still think we owe the fans because they have been very supportive and we’ve had much better results away from home than at home. This is a big game for everyone in the club and we wanted to give them a big win.”

#778. What's going on with the polar vortex?

Observations show the ring of fierce winds that rotate at the Earth's North Pole has changed direction. Scientists say it's a historic disruption and the earliest reversal on record. What could it mean for the weather?

High up in the atmosphere, there's a ring of cold air swirling over the Arctic that can intensify, weaken, and shapeshift through the seasons. This is the polar vortex.

If it gets disrupted, this twisting pool of chilly air can influence the weather we experience, increasing the risk of a cold snap in the Northern Hemisphere.

Current observations show the vortex has weakened unprecedentedly early this year, with its winds reversing directions.

It's not yet clear how the current disruption to the polar vortex will affect the Northern Hemisphere winter, but scientists agree it is a record-breaking event.

"As far as we know, this is the earliest stratospheric vortex disruption that has been observed," European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecast (ECMWF) principal scientists Tim Stockdale and Frederic Vitart told the AFP news agency.

The French meteorological agency Meteo-France, meanwhile, called it "an unprecedented event."

The early breakdown of the vortex "really increases the chance of cold air outbreaks across the latitudes where most of the densely populated population centers are across the Northern Hemisphere, US, Europe and East Asia," Judah Cohen, a climatologist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology told AFP.

The polar vortex is an enormous band of cold, low-pressure air that spins counterclockwise around the North Pole, about 10 to 50 kilometers (around 6 to 30 miles) above the surface.

It's closely connected to the jet stream, another band of powerful winds just below the vortex. The jet stream forms a boundary where the cold Arctic air meets warmer air from the tropics and subtropics.

The vortex can sometimes be a tight circle, keeping the coldest air locked around the North Pole over winter. It can also form uneven waves that dip southwards. And as it changes in strength and shape, that can influence the atmosphere below and alter the position of the jet stream, which drives the weather on the ground.

So, if the jet stream is more "wavy," and plunges south, it may also allow freezing Arctic air to spill southward.

One of the biggest influences that can provoke this kind of disruption is known as "sudden stratospheric warming." This is when temperatures in the polar stratosphere rise dramatically within a few days, causing the vortex's strong westerly winds to weaken.

This can push the vortex off its spot at the North Pole, make it split apart into multiple rings, or — as is happening now — cause the westerly winds to change direction.

It can take several weeks for the vortex to recover.

A previous polar vortex disruption contributed to the deadly Great Texas Freeze in February 2021, which caused more than a week of freezing temperatures that sparked power outages and killed hundreds of people.

But bone-chilling cold isn't a foregone conclusion. The Met Office, which is the UK's national weather and climate service, stresses that what's happening with the polar vortex can nudge odds in that direction, but it's not a switch that turns cold weather on and off.

Other weather patterns can also influence the outcome.

For example, there's a possibility El Nino, which is associated with milder winters, could "moderate or modify" the impacts, Cohen told AFP. But he added this was not certain.

The El Nino weather phenomenon, caused by the warming of surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is currently intensifying and is expected to peak at the end of the year. The ongoing event has been classified as exceptionally strong and is disrupting weather around the globe.

Some research has also linked the rapid warming of the Arctic driven by climate change to increasing disruptions to the polar vortex. That means that, even as the planet warms, some areas may still experience more severe cold spells. But this connection is not conclusive and is still debated by scientists.

#777. Miley Cyrus’ Wedding Dress Revealed: Details on Her Backless Gown

Miley Cyrus wore a stunning long-sleeved gown for her and Maxx Morando’s Palm Springs wedding, where she said "I do" in front of mom Tish Cyrus, dad Billy Ray Cyrus and more.

Miley Cyrus’ wedding dress is one in a million.

The Hannah Montana alum tied the knot with Maxx Morando in Palm Springs, Calif., Nov. 21 after five years of dating. And while the ceremony was an emotional affair for everyone in attendance, it was Miley’s dress that stole the show like a wrecking ball.

The 33-year-old was a vision in white as she donned a long-sleeved, backless gown designed by Saint Laurent by Anthony Vaccarello to exchange vows with Maxx, according to photos of the newlyweds, shot by photographer Jose Villa, which Miley shared on Instagram Nov. 22.

To really allow the most-wanted gown to shine, the 33-year-old wore her hair in a tousled up-do.

And it’s clear the nuptials were something beautiful as photos from the ceremony showed Miley wiping away tears as she stood in front of the Liily drummer, per photos obtained by DeuxMoi.

As for the loved ones who watched their butterflies fly away to a new chapter, Miley’s mom Tish Cyrus and stepdad Dominic Purcell were just two family members who witnessed Miley and Maxx throw down their vows.

Additionally, her sisters Brandi Cyrus and Noah Cyrus watched on as the “Flowers” singer proved her heart beats for love. Plus, Miley’s father Billy Ray Cyrus and his partner Elizabeth Hurley did the same alongside Elizabeth's son Damien Hurley.

One night before the ceremony, Miley’s stepsister Lily-Rose Purcell shared special details from the couple’s rehearsal dinner Nov. 20.

In fact, she shared a close-up of the event’s dinner menu on Instagram Stories, which included a main course of filet mignon and Maine lobster ravioli, followed by a dessert selection of chocolate caramel layer cake, vanilla crème brûlée and raspberry sorbet.

But the breakout detail had to be the “M+M” printed at the top of the menu—a nod to the couple’s first initials.

Maxx, 28, and Miley began dating in 2021 after a mutual friend set them up on a blind date. Four years later, the pair confirmed their engagement in December 2025 after the “Toro” musician popped the question during a vacation in Japan.

"I’m not totally the boss in our house," Miley told Zane Lowe in an interview shared by Apple Music Sept. 17. "It's like a sense of relief that I can actually soften into, because he’s going to watch this and be like, 'You’re not the boss. We’re both the boss.'"

And it’s that playful banter that she’s especially excited to bring into their marriage.

As she put it, "I think that’s the thing that maybe generations prior didn’t teach us, that marriage doesn’t need to be a prison. It can actually be a playground."

Keep reading for a closer look into Miley and Maxx’s love story…

Miley Cyrus and musician Maxx Morando began dating in 2021. "We got put on a blind date," she recalled to British Vogue in 2023. "Well, it was blind for me and not really for him. I thought, 'The worst that can happen is I leave.'"

Miley didn't leave and, as their romance blossomed, the pair went red carpet official at the Gucci Love Parade event on November 2, 2021.

Miley and Maxx, who is a drummer in the band Liily, enjoyed a night out seeing Chicago on Broadway.

The "Flowers" singer and her boyfriend stepped out together at a Versace runway show in West Hollywood on March 9, 2023.

Maxx was by Miley's side when she won her first-ever Grammy at the 2024 award ceremony. The couple even shared a sweet smooch at their table during the event, and Miley referred to Maxx in her acceptance speech as "my love."

They returned to the Grammy Awards in 2025 for another public date night. "He’s very similar to me," Miley told Harper's Bazaar in an interview published November 2024. "We just don’t take life too seriously."

Maxx, who is six years younger than the Hannah Montana star, joined Miley on the red carpet at SNL50: The Anniversary Special, to celebrate 50 years of Saturday Night Live.

The musicians got glammed up for a big night out at the 2025 Oscars ceremony.

And later that night they stepped out in fresh looks for an appearance at the Vanity Fair Oscar Party.

It was a party in the U.S.A. when the pair got married in Plam Springs.

#776. Spurs 'a match for anyone' as win at Man City boosts European hopes

Spurs secure famous win as Man City falter again

Dreams of reaching the Women's Champions League may have seemed fanciful for Tottenham Hotspur when the season began.

The Women's Super League has an established big four, and big-spending London City Lionesses were the side making the most obvious play to disrupt that dominance.

But a hugely impressive and deserved win at Manchester City on Sunday afternoon proves Spurs are a team on the up, and the table shows they remain firmly in top-three contention.

Two late goals secured a 3-1 win at Joie Stadium, but this was no smash-and-grab job. Spurs were more dynamic than sluggish City, pressing them into submission.

They restricted their hosts' stellar attack to precious few chances and took the ones they created.

"When we are on our game, we can be a match for anyone," Spurs manager Martin Ho said in his post-match media conference.

"It gives us confidence - but it is just one game."

Man City beaten by Spurs and miss chance to go top of WSL

Victory kept Spurs, whose highest finish in the WSL is fifth, firmly in the mix this time.

They are fifth again, but just three points behind London City Lionesses who occupy the final European place as the league heads into a last international break of 2026.

Chelsea lead the way from Manchester City, with Manchester United one point ahead of Tottenham, who in turn sit handily clear of their sixth-placed north London rivals Arsenal.

The big four are therefore all present in the top six. London City are right there, too, and Spurs, with six wins from 11 games so far, are gamely pressing their own case.

What made Sunday's win and performance from Tottenham even more impressive is how dreadful their recent record against Manchester City had been.

Tottenham had lost six of their previous seven away matches against City in all competitions, averaging over four goals conceded per defeat.

Last season City won this fixture 5-2 with Khadija Shaw scoring a 13-minute hat-trick, the quickest in WSL history.

Shaw's early goal on Sunday, her 16th in league matches versus Spurs, could easily have started a landslide.

That was expected. City had won each of their past 17 WSL home games, including all 10 in 2026 â until Tottenham tore up the script.

The outcome means Manchester City, beaten at Chelsea in their previous outing, have suffered consecutive league losses for the first time since January 2025.

Spurs have rediscovered form after losing all three league games in October while conceding 14 goals

Tottenham's victory came down to Ho's brave tactics and his team's superb execution of them.

After going behind, they pressed City constantly, forcing errors and creating chances. That tenacity won them countless one-on-ones, with City unable or unwilling to play over the press.

After her goal, Shaw was rendered anonymous by the hard work and close marking of centre-backs Toko Koga and Amanda Nilden.

Down the right, Kirsty Hanson dominated Carlotta Wamser, could have been awarded a penalty and provided the low cross for Cathinka Tandberg's equaliser.

In midfield, Drew Spence pulled all the strings and covered the entire pitch. At 34, she is perhaps playing the best football of her career and deserved her assist for the winner. After Matilda Vinberg put Spurs in front, several players ran to celebrate with Spence.

"When you come into this, you wonder if it will go against you, but the players were outstanding," said Ho.

"We haven't won here in so long, so we know it will be a tough game, but I have belief in my team when we are on song. I thought we were outstanding - we worked every blade of grass."

Spurs are clearly capable of taking the game to anyone in the league and have now scored 28 WSL goals this season, with only Chelsea and London City having more.

In the second half they adapted to City sending on such fluid attacking threats as Mary Fowler, Kerstin Casperij and Beth Mead.

They lifted the gas from the press, applying it more sparingly, and were solid in defence.

It shows that Ho has learned painful lessons from the past - whether from Spurs' poor record against City, including two five-goal losses in 2025-26, or conceding six to Chelsea and London City back to back in October.

"We have maybe been naive at times and I own that, so we are more reserved," Ho said of his tactical approach. "It was managing that, and the players' communication was excellent."

City were limited to fleeting chances. Jade Rose blasting over after keeper Lize Kop parried a Lauren Hemp free-kick was as close as they came to a second goal, and those were their first shots after a 50-minute drought.

When Spurs got their late chances through the hard work of Vinberg, they could strike for three points.

Vinberg had quite the rollercoaster afternoon. She was initially named on the bench but was promoted to the starting XI 15 minutes before kick-off as Olivia Holdt was suffering stomach cramps.

Perhaps unprepared, she gave away the ball playing out of defence leading to City's opener. But she grew into the game, scored Spurs' second goal and set up Jess Naz for the third.

It was a great moment for Naz, on her 100th WSL appearance of a career that has been disrupted by injury.

Spurs are back in Manchester before Christmas, visiting United on 20 December.

There will be real hope of a positive result as they press their way into contention for what would be a historic achievement of a top-three finish.

#775. Net zero emissions won’t reverse climate change — some nations look to ‘net negative’

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

A display reminds those attending the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, of their goal: limiting global warming to 1.5 ºC.Credit: Metin Aktas/Anadolu/Getty

Net zero is no longer enough. Among countries at the COP31 climate summit under way in Antalya, Turkey, there’s a growing recognition that meeting climate targets will require the world to go ‘net negative’, which means removal of more carbon dioxide from the air than is added.

Scientists say that climate ‘overshoot’ — exceeding 1.5 °C of warming, a target set in 2015 in the landmark Paris agreement — is now inevitable in the next few years. Reaching net-zero status would halt the rise in temperatures. But only achieving net-negative status can bring temperatures back below the 1.5 °C threshold this century.

Can AI actually help the climate? Nations want to harness the technology to cut emissions

Can AI actually help the climate? Nations want to harness the technology to cut emissions

That reality has made net negative and the enormous amount of CO2 removal that would be needed to achieve it a prominent idea at the summit. A coalition of eight countries called the Group of Negative Emitters (GONE) has been working to convince other nations to adopt net-negative targets and get serious about CO2 removal. The group announced that it will be co-chaired by Denmark and Ethiopia, which is hosting next year’s climate summit and could put net negative at the top of the agenda.

“We are in an era of overshoot, and we have to do a lot in terms of removing carbon dioxide,” Ethiopian ambassador Samuel Addis Alemayehu said at a GONE event on 18 November, touting the nation’s progress on reforestation.

Some climate campaigners worry that CO2 removal technologies won’t work and that focusing on them could distract countries from cutting emissions. Despite those concerns, the latest draft of the main statement from COP31 recognizes that CO2 removal has a role in addressing the overshoot, and welcomes efforts to “urgently and rapidly” scale up development of removal methods.

According to a United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) report1 released ahead of the meeting, the world can expect about 1.8 °C of warming this century, even in the most optimistic emissions scenario.

Every fraction of a degree above 1.5 °C raises the risk of climate disasters such as wildfires and powerful hurricanes. “COP31 will be judged a failure if we don’t address the overshoot,” said Ilana Seid, Palau’s ambassador to the UN and chair of the Association of Small Island States, at a press briefing held during the summit.

Many countries at the meeting have discussed slashing emissions to limit the size and duration of the coming overshoot. Turkey has pushed to implement a target of 35% of global energy demand being met with electricity by 2035, a proposal that has gained support from more than 75 countries at the conference and is also included in the draft statement.

But the UNEP report estimates that to recover from overshoot, at least 330 billion tonnes of CO2 would have to be pulled out of the atmosphere this century after the world reaches net zero. Removing that much CO2 would require a vast expansion of existing efforts. Today, about two billion tonnes of CO2 per year are removed by nature-based projects such as reforestation, which takes advantage of the carbon absorbed by growing trees. Scaling up carbon removal quickly enough to achieve net negative and storing carbon in a more durable form will require technological CO2 removal solutions as well.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03789-3

United Nations Environment Programme. Limiting Overshoot: Navigating Exceedance of 1.5°C and Pathways Towards Return (UNEP, 2026).

#773. Selena Gomez Helps Couple With Baby’s Sex Reveal at Spurs Game, ‘With No Hesitation’

The star opened the envelope and announced whether the baby will be born male or female at Saturday night's game in San Antonio, Texas.

Selena Gomez happily announced whether a boy or girl is to be expected for a pregnant fan she ran into at the Spurs-Pelicans basketball game this weekend in San Antonio.

A short video of the precious moment from Saturday night’s (Nov. 21) NBA match between San Antonio and New Orleans started popping up across social media on Sunday. Filmed at the Texas city’s Frost Bank Center, the footage was originally posted online by the expectant couple around midnight local time. The clip shows Gomez opening a sealed envelope containing the big reveal.

Carefully scanning over the paper that listed the sex assigned to the baby, a smiling Gomez slowly said, “You’re … How do I know? … FEMALE!” Then she gave the mom and dad a big hug.

“I cannot put into words just how special this night was!” wrote game attendee/mom @laurenicoleramz on Instagram. “We are expecting baby #4 so soon, already starting the third trimester & planning to wait until birth for our last to find out our gender. We decided to bring our envelope in case we could get someone to open it for us, & the sweetest @selenagomez did that with no hesitation!!”

Captioning the snapshot and personal video clip with Gomez (seen here), she shared: “She was so sweet & it felt so natural just to talk to her because of her gentle & kind personality. Thank you @selenagomez & @spurs for making this a night to remember!! Swipe to see/hear what baby #4 is!! So thankful to God for this sweet baby that will complete our family!!”

Gomez also posed for a picture during their meeting, resting her hand on the mama’s belly.

The star appeared to be in good spirits at the game, where she was also gifted a jersey by the San Antonio Spurs Coyote, the team’s official mascot.

The Spurs defeated the Pelicans 114-91. When Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama was asked about Gomez’s appearance watching the game Saturday night, he quipped, “I had to show off for Selena, you know.”

Gomez’s new trailer for season six of Only Murders in the Building — this season with an Only Murders in London theme — co-starring Steve Martin and Martin Short, arrived last week. The hit Hulu crime comedy returns with its season premiere on Dec. 8.

Tallulah Willis detailed her regret over sharing a personal photo of her dad Bruce Willis as he continues to battle a form of dementia: "I can acknowledge that and vow to do better.”

Tallulah Willis is always in her father Bruce Willis’ corner.

One day after the 32-year-old shared a sweet father-daughter photo with The Sixth Sense star, who is currently battling a form of dementia, she explained why she ultimately felt it best to delete the snap.

“I posted a photo of my dad yesterday because we were having a BEAUTIFUL visit,” she wrote on Instagram Nov. 22 alongside a throwback photo with her dad. “I had someone take a super sweet photo of a shared moment between us watching a video of Frankie Valli singing.”

“I was very excited by the sweetness of the moment that I didn't think farther ahead that this was possibly too intimate a photo to show,” she added. “I can acknowledge that and vow to do better.”

In the now-deleted photo shared to her Instagram Nov. 21, Tallulah—who Bruce shares with ex-wife Demi Moore alongside daughters Rumer Willis, 38, and Scout Willis, 35—sat next to the 71-year-old on an outdoor porch swing as they held hands.

While Tallulah wore a red sweater, jeans and sunglasses as she wrapped one arm around the Die Hard star, he wore a gray cardigan and a pale pink shirt.

Though Tallulah decided it best to keep the memory between the pair of them, she acknowledged that she knows how much her updates mean to his fans.

“I know you all love him,” she added. “I love him. My family loves him. And he's still always the absolute hero we know him to be.”

She captioned the post, “I can do better.”

Bruce’s family shared he was diagnosed with FTD—an umbrella term for diseases that affect the frontal and temporal lobes of the brain, which are associated with personality and behavior, per Mayo Clinic—in 2023.

And recently, his wife Emma Heming Willis offered deeper insight into how the Willis family is coping with their new normal.

“It is extremely difficult and painful,” Emma—mom kids Mabel, 14, and Evelyn, 12, with Bruce—told Hello! In an interview published Sept. 7. “It's natural, we all want our loved ones to be healthy, full of life and being the person they always were. But FTD is a devastating illness that steals things from you very slowly. So the reality is that you find yourself constantly in a state of grief.”

But the dark chapter has been made brighter with the Willis women by her side.

“What has been truly beautiful to see throughout this process is how we all pour our hearts into supporting him—how deeply we love him, while completely respecting the way each person chooses to express that love,” she explained. “I think the balance we've found is simply a reflection of who Bruce is at his core; it’s the result of all the love and support he planted over the years coming right back to him now.”

Bruce received a big cuddle from his three oldest daughters and Demi in 2025.

"You are the funniest, most tender, charming, out of this world silly talented and magical papa. Looking through these photos this morning I am just filled with the deepest gratitude that we chose to spend this life together. I am your first baby and man sometimes I wish I could be tiny enough to just cozy up on your chest again and laugh and cuddle you."

#771. Fifa to confirm UK as host for 2035 Women's World Cup

Spain beat England 1-0 to win the 2023 World Cup

Fifa is set to confirm on Monday that a first football World Cup will be hosted in the United Kingdom since 1966.

England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales are the only bidders to jointly stage the 2035 Women's World Cup.

A delegation will be present at Fifa's Zurich headquarters with national associations holding a specially arranged virtual meeting, and voting to ratify the co-hosts.

The tournament would involve 104 matches contested by 48 teams over 39 days.

Nineteen venues are proposed by the 'All Together' bid, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales.

Fifa's evaluation of the bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five. However, its contractual framework was rated 'medium risk', and the document claimed that "certain government guarantees contain material qualifications, particularly regarding tax and safety and security".

This is thought to refer to a lack of agreement over a request by Fifa for tax-free status for all football-related activities.

Fifa's bid evaluation said: "The bidder has submitted an extensive set of government support documents and contractual hosting agreements, demonstrating the commitment of the relevant authorities and stakeholders.

"However, certain government guarantees, particularly those relating to safety and security and tax, contain certain qualifications which have been duly noted in the legal evaluation.

"While certain contractual matters remain subject to further discussion, the bidder's proactive engagement with Fifa and the substantial lead-in time provide a sound basis for resolving these outstanding issues."

Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium is one of 19 stadiums included in the 2035 bid

England hosted the women's European Championship in 2022, which the Lionesses won.

England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland are also joint hosts of the men's European Championship in 2028.

Mark Bullingham, chief executive of the Football Association, said: "Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play.

"Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations."

The English stadiums included in the 2035 bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, the Stadium of Light and Old Trafford.

If Manchester United's proposed new Old Trafford stadium does not go ahead, it will still be considered in its current form.

A further three stadiums could be added - Birmingham's new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham's redeveloped Racecourse Ground and a potential new Chelsea ground - which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 venues.

The Principality Stadium in Cardiff is one of two Welsh venues, along with the Cardiff City Stadium

Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium the two Welsh venues.

Noel Mooney, the chief executive of the Football Association of Wales, said: "Wales has been a football nation for 150 years and we have never hosted anything on this scale. World Cup football played here, in front of Welsh children, would change what this game looks like in Wales: in the clubs, in the schools, and in the number of girls who grow up seeing a pathway into it."

Northern Ireland missed out on co-hosting the men's Euros in 2028 after the UK government said in 2024 it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time for the tournament - but a redeveloped Windsor Park is set to stage matches in 2035.

The Irish Football Association's chief executive Patrick Nelson said the event "would be felt in every club and every age group, in every part of the country. Our young players would grow up having watched the best in the world play at home, and there is no substitute for that."

Easter Road in Edinburgh and Hampden Park in Glasgow are the Scottish venues proposed, with Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell saying hosting the tournament would be "the most significant thing to happen to the women's and girls' game in Scotland".

He added: "The impact would go far beyond just the matches themselves. The level of investment into coaching, facilities and player pathways in the years beforehand will shape the future of the game for the generations to come."

The special meeting of Fifa's Congress is also set to approve the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.

#769. The dangers of revising Europe's security architecture

Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework because they say it would mean granting Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.

European leaders have so far found compromises in response to many of US President Donald Trump's demands.

But they were surprised to hear Trump say that he raised Europe's security framework with Russian officials.

"It's going to be a big agreement and it's going to involve more than Ukraine," Trump said after meeting Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House last week.

He said that deal might include all of Europe. But what he meant by "all of Europe" was not clear.

US envoy Jared Kushner also wrote that Europe and Russia had struggled to establish a sustainable security framework for more than 30 years and that he was looking at "broader" European security architecture before he was to fly to Abu Dhabi.

That sent off alarm bells in European capitals, with diplomats having pushed back on Washington's approach to secure a peace deal in Ukraine.

They feared that a peace settlement could restore Russia's sphere of influence and undermine NATO.

"We ​already have European security ​architecture in place. NATO and the European Union both have their ​respective roles. We ​must make sure Ukraine is integrated ‌into ⁠this architecture," said Kaja Kallas, the European Union's foreign policy chief.

Russia made clear during talks in Abu Dhabi earlier this week that they were keen to discuss a broader European security framework before tackling the specifics of the war.

"Phrases about the European security architecture are certainly Russian talking points and not only talking points but, to a degree, part of a media propaganda effort that Russia makes to frame the war as it wishes to frame the war," said Michael Kimmage, a historian of the Cold War.

Russian leaders, including Vladimir Putin, have long alleged that the US and NATO repeatedly violated pledges they made in the early 1990s not to expand the alliance into the former Soviet bloc.

They have seen NATO's enlargement during this period as having put them in a humiliating position in which they could do very little.

At the same time, in the 1990s, the European project saw the birth of the European Union, the single market that ensured the free movement of goods and people across member states, the Schengen agreement for border-free travel, and the euro.

The core idea was to extend peace across the continent.

"Europe can mean so many things, but the European project was not designed for war. It was designed for peace," said Kimmage.

During this period, there were even suggestions of Russia becoming a NATO member.

But that relative period of stability changed after Russia invaded Georgia in 2008, annexed Crimea in 2014 and launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

"Russia wants to redraw all of this by force. And I think that that's fundamentally unacceptable to Europe with all the diversity and variations that you get within the European landscape on what's acceptable and not acceptable. I think the large-scale redrawing of borders by force is just not the European project," said Kimmage.

"So to the extent that the redrawing of borders by force is the lifeblood of Russian foreign policy, and I think that's a pretty easy case to make, Russia and Europe are at an impasse," he said.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The Trump administration very quickly turned to making sure that "existing European security institutions" would be intact, with Jared Kushner having said late Thursday that the next round of negotiations would include "our European partners."

Kushner, along with Steve Witkoff, flew to Moscow to talk to Putin after talks in Abu Dhabi. Then they flew to Dublin, Ireland, to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Kushner had earlier Thursday signaled some "really incredible" postwar plans for Ukraine, saying that it could not be concluded without Europeans at the table.

"We should not allow a diktat from Russia that would result in some kind of neutralization or significant reduction in the military forces of Ukraine going forward, because that would make Ukraine very, very vulnerable to future aggression and pressure coming from Russia," said Hiski Haukkala, the director of the Finnish Institute of International Affairs.

That would mean that Ukraine would also be completely dependent on the security guarantees that the US or Europeans are able and willing to provide.

"We are supporting Ukraine because we are supporting international law and the basic norms of decency and international security when it comes to European security architecture. And this is the vantage point from which we are operating," he said.

The European Union has repeatedly pointed to some of the basic treaties that Russia broke, including:

"Russia walked away from these principles and smashed them to pieces in the process. And they are not interested in reinstating the previous security architecture order. They want something different in its stead. And as long as this is not on the table, the Russian form of negotiation is to wage war. War is a form of bargaining," Haukkala said.

"And they are signaling strategic intent to change the makeup of European security, to subdue Ukraine and to change the very essence of European security," he added.

Daniel Fried, a former assistant secretary of state for European Affairs in the George W. Bush administration, said Russia is very good at sticking to its demands.

He said Russians know how to negotiate and "right now, they are not negotiating," referring to talks in Abu Dhabi.

Some experts said there was no possibility of having a new security architecture with the Russians at this point because there was no trust or common vision to align with Russia at the moment.

"There is no obvious compromise — dismantling NATO and the EU is not an option for Europe," said Maria Snegovaya, an expert on Russia at the Center for Strategic and International Studies think tank.

"Repeatedly offering Putin peace deals he is unwilling to accept will not produce that outcome," Snegovaya said.

Others like Balazs Jarabik, an expert on post-Soviet politics, said that Russia was part of the European security architecture whether Europeans liked it or not.

"And the question is whether it's included as our enemy. Obviously, Russia is not going to be a partner, right? We have to find a modus operandi to reduce the risk of a horizontal escalation and potentially a bigger European war, even a bigger one than what we have now."

A host of European leaders on Friday rejected the Russian demands to discuss Europe's security framework as well, with a spokesperson for the German government saying that Berlin was looking to host a meeting of the "Coalition of the Willing" to secure funding for Ukraine's defense and reach a unified position regarding future peace talks.

#768. From conceding seven to Hull heroics - how Tzolakis recovered to defy Brighton

McBurnie stoppage-time double earns Hull win over 10-man Brighton

Hull boss Sergej Jakirovic used one word to describe the performance of his goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis in Sunday's 2-0 Premier League win against Brighton.

"Unbelievable," he told Match of the Day.

"Especially after the international break, which was very difficult for him."

Tzolakis' previous outing had been for Greece against the Netherlands in the Uefa Nations League, where he and his side were humbled 7-0 by the hosts in Amsterdam.

Nine days later, his contribution to the Tigers' first league victory since 29 August was every bit as important as that of striker Oli McBurnie, who netted both goals in second-half stoppage time against the second-placed Seagulls.

Tzolakis made a series of top saves to keep the highest scorers in the top flight at bay and, when Brighton full-back Costinha was sent off in the 89th minute for a second bookable offence, the hosts seized their opportunity to clinch only their third win following their Premier League return.

McBurnie said the 24-year-old stopper had "kept Hull in a few games" this season and the club were "lucky to have him", while Tzolakis told Sky Sports: "We are a unit and a team.

"We play for each other. We showed a good team effort and we deserved the three points."

McBurnie scores stoppage-time double as Hull stun Brighton

How 'outstanding' Tzolakis kept Brighton at bay

With the opportunity to move three points behind leaders Arsenal, Brighton looked most likely to score for long spells of Sunday's game, but just could not find a way past former Olympiacos goalkeeper Tzolakis, who joined Hull in August for a reported Â£20m fee.

He got down to make a vital block early on to deny Diego Gomez, who had slid in to meet a low cross from the left wing. It was the first of several occasions the Paraguay international would be frustrated in front of goal.

Tzolakis then raced out spreadeagled to foil Georginio Rutter with an outstretched left hand - a stop that BBC Radio 5 Live pundit and former striker Clinton Morrison described as "Peter Schmeichel-esque", referring to the legendary Denmark keeper.

Second-half efforts from distance by Pascal Gross and Lewis Dunk were dealt with, too.

Yasin Ayari went close with a thumping strike against the bar and when Brighton substitute Charalampos Kostoulas pounced on a short backpass to go through one-on-one, Tzolakis got a hand on his Greece team-mate's shot and Regan Slater was back on the goalline to head the ball to safety.

Former Liverpool midfielder Danny Murphy, a pundit on Sunday's Match of the Day, said: "We saw again how important Tzolakis is for Hull. He had one of those days where he was always in the right place at the right time.

"When you are a Hull player and you see the kind of saves Tzolakis made when he spread himself and kept it out with his foot, you start thinking that it could be your day.

"It happens a lot in football and, on the flip side, Brighton will have been thinking, 'are we ever going to score here?'."

Hull made a superb start to the campaign after being promoted via the Championship play-offs in May.

They followed victories against Manchester United and Coventry with a draw against Aston Villa - all without conceding a goal.

The Tigers had not won since that 1-0 success at Coventry until beating Brighton - but they are one of four top-flight sides still unbeaten at home and have not lost any fixture by more than a one-goal margin.

They lost 1-0 to champions Arsenal before the international break and Scotland forward McBurnie told Match of the Day: "We know we can make it difficult for the top teams in the league and we've proved that in the past two games.

"We want to make it as difficult as we can for teams to come here and make the MKM Stadium a tough place to come. It's proving that way so far, so long may it continue."

#767. Miley Cyrus & Maxx Morando’s Wedding Photos Are Here

The couple were married in Palm Springs, Calif., on Saturday (Nov. 21).

Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando’s wedding pictures are here. The bride and groom shared the first official look at their marriage ceremony on Sunday, the day after their intimate Saturday (Nov. 21) event in Palm Springs, Calif.

Cyrus posted four wedding photos on Instagram along with the caption “M + M 11.21.26” surrounding a white heart emoji. Photographer Jose Villa was credited for the images.

The newlyweds’ portraits are in black and white, matching the timeless elegance of Cyrus’ long-sleeved, silk Saint Laurent gown with a train and Morando’s classic black tux — which he accessorized with his signature dark shades. The couple are seen embracing in the romantic shots, and in one photo they’re joined by a presumed member of the family: a sweet dog lying comfortably at their feet.

Paparazzi footage of Cyrus, 33, and Morando, 28, getting married poolside, at a former residence of Frank Sinatra — that captured an apparently emotional Cyrus wiping away tears as she and her soon-to-be husband stood in front of their loved ones to say “I do” — made it online Saturday night.

Other family members from the Cyrus family spotted at the wedding were Miley’s dad, Billy Ray with partner Elizabeth Hurley; her mom, Tish, with husband Dominic Purcell, and her sister Noah.

Flaming Lips frontman Wayne Coyne, a longtime collaborator and friend of Cyrus, reportedly served as officiant at the ceremony.

Cyrus’ wedding dress was designed by Anthony Vaccarello for Saint Laurent; Morando also wore Saint Laurent, according to People.

Cyrus was first linked to Morando, who’s the drummer for Los Angeles rock band Liily, in 2021. He co-starred in the lovey-dovey music video for Miley’s “Let’s Get Married,” a single from the star’s latest No. 1, her Billboard 200 chart-topping 2026 album Bass Persuades.

#766. 90 Day Fiancé Alum Sheila Mangubat Dead at 35

90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days alum Sheila Mangubat has died at the age of 35, her former fiancé David Dangerfield confirmed: “I am devastated and still trying to process this loss.”

90 Day Fiancé fans are mourning a heartbreaking loss.

Sheila Mangubat—who appeared on 90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days in 2023—died in the Philippines on Nov. 21, her former fiancé David Dangerfield confirmed. She died just days before her 36th birthday, according to TMZ.

“It breaks my heart to share the news from her family that Sheila passed away on Saturday in the Philippines,” David wrote on Instagram Nov. 21 alongside a black-and-white photo of Sheila. “I am devastated and still trying to process this loss.”

“Please keep her son, her family, and me in your prayers,” the 45-year-old added. “Thank you for all your love and support.”

Sheila’s cause of death has not yet been confirmed.

As the reality star’s loved ones begin to grieve, her brother Jonathan Mangubat shared footage from Sheila’s funeral to his Facebook Stories Nov. 22, per TMZ, while her sister Grace Mangubat paid tribute to her late sibling on her own social media.

“Rest in peace my beloved sister,” she wrote on Facebook Nov. 21. “Sorry kaau layo kaau ko, dili ko kauli DHA.”

“Fly high my Sister,” she added. “We will miss you.”

Sheila and David’s romance was documented on season six of TLC’s 90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days in 2023. After meeting in a Facebook group for deaf singles in 2021, the pair sparked a long-distance romance, before becoming engaged. The former couple’s time on the show concluded with Sheila accepting David’s proposal.

In October 2025, Sheila and David broke up due to distance and K-1 visa issues, but rekindled their relationship in June, according to TMZ.

But David, who was born deaf, expressed that his love of Sheila—mom to son Jhonreil from a previous relationship—is eternal.

“I’m happy I never gave up because I found my love,” he shared on a June 2023 episode of Before the 90 Days. “I have a girlfriend whose name is Sheila, and she’s beautiful. She is 31 and lives in Cebu, Philippines. When I first saw Sheila’s picture, it got my heart beating.”

At the time, David saw forever in the TLC star.

“I will have a new family with Sheila in the future,” he vowed. “Sheila is better than any other woman I’ve dated because Sheila is a sweet person. She is the perfect match to me. I’ll love Sheila forever.”

#765. The red card that changed Liverpool-Man Utd: correct call?

Ngumoha stars as Liverpool thrash 10-man Man Utd

Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card was a pivotal moment early in Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Manchester United boss.

It handed Liverpool the initiative at Anfield, and Andoni Iraola's players took advantage by scoring two goals in quick succession.

Was there a case for the video assistant referee (VAR) to suggest it should be downgraded to a yellow?

Let's take a look at the incident, and what a referee takes into account before showing a red for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

Photographers at Anfield captured the sequence of events - from challenge to red card

Photographers at Anfield captured the sequence of events - from challenge to red card

Photographers at Anfield captured the sequence of events - from challenge to red card

Photographers at Anfield captured the sequence of events - from challenge to red card

Photographers at Anfield captured the sequence of events - from challenge to red card

Ronald Araujo played a long ball upfield for Alexander Isak to run on to.

Isak took a touch, before Yoro bundled into the back of the Sweden international and brought him down.

Referee Sam Barrott did not hesitate, giving the foul and sending off Yoro.

Was there doubt that Isak would have taken control of the ball? If so, it should only be a caution.

There are four key considerations for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity:

distance between the offence and the goal

likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball

location and number of defenders and attackers

As Isak was running directly towards goal in a central position, and there was no covering defender, three of the factors were satisfied.

The question is about the "likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball".

The Liverpool striker took a heavy touch, which moved the ball a few yards ahead of him.

The touch came before contact from Yoro, so there is no case that the challenge caused Isak to over-run the ball.

The referee and the VAR, John Brooks, must therefore assess whether Isak would definitely have got to the ball ahead of Senne Lammens. And that if he had, it would have been a good scoring chance.

If there is any doubt, then it should not be a red card.

It is a borderline case, and as such the VAR would not be expected to intervene for a clear and obvious error.

Likewise, if the referee had shown a yellow the VAR would not get involved.

Former Liverpool and England midfielder Danny Murphy, who is a pundit on Sunday's Match of the Day, said there was "no doubt" about the red card.

Former Manchester United defender Gary Neville also agreed with the decision.

"Leny Yoro has to cover and he doesn't," Neville said on Sky Sports. "He reacts late and his anticipation is poor.

"It's so clumsy from Yoro. It's naivety, he just needs to get off the pitch. You're not going to get that turned around, no chance."

But for Liverpool boss Iraola the decision is not up for debate.

"I think he's the last man, no?" he said. "It's a clear foul and a red card, yes?

Did Liverpool 'get lucky' with red card decision?

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes felt it should not have been a red card and said the decision had a detrimental impact on the game.

"It's one that needs to be looked at," Fernandes told Sky Sports.

"We have far too many meetings with the referees for this to happen to us again. The last one against Chelsea [when Lisandro Martinez was sent off], you can give it as a red card and it was probably a second yellow also. Today, you can't give a red card.

"It's very clear they show us if the player is not in control of the ball, it's never a red card.

"Isak kicks the ball forward, the ball goes into the hands of Senne. Isak has got no control of the ball, he has no chance to get on the ball. He puts his leg across to try to get some advantage from Leny. I can understand the fall, but it's never a red card.

"There are too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR taking so long to see to make a mistake like this that can change the game.

"It's not because of them we conceded the goal from the free-kick, but it changes the game completely."

Pochettino, meanwhile, was frustrated by what he perceived as inconsistency in the decision-making of the officials.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss felt his new team should have been awarded a penalty moments before Yoro was sent off, after Jeremy Jacquet went shoulder to shoulder with Bryan Mbeumo.

"It's difficult to accept that because it was a foul under my view and for me was a penalty," Pochettino told Match of the Day.

"Look how everything changes if that action was a red card and a foul, I think we need to review. When I played football that situation is normal. The action against Mbeumo, if that [Yoro foul on Isak] was a red card then that was a penalty."

'We have too many referees' - Fernandes disagrees with Yoro red

There have been a couple of very similar cases this season.

Brighton's Pascal Struijk was sent off at Sunderland through a VAR review after he brought down Wilson Isidor.

The Seagulls successfully appealed against that red card on the grounds that there was clear doubt that Isidor would have taken control of the ball before it ran through to goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

Could Manchester United appeal against Yoro's red card? There's nothing to lose by doing so.

Despite the Football Association regulatory commission unanimously ruling the Struijk red card was wrong, the Premier League's key match incidents panel voted the VAR intervention was a correct call on a split 3-2 vote.

Ipswich's Issa Diop avoided a VAR red card for a foul on James McAtee against Nottingham Forest, when the referee disagreed with the video official, and believed there was a covering defender. Forest boss Oliver Glasner was adamant it had been a clear goalscoring opportunity.

It was the same referee, Thomas Bramall, for both of those incidents.

That shows just how subjective such decisions can be. It is often rare to get a real consensus.

Yoro can count himself a little unfortunate to get the red card.

#764. Legendary Jewelry Designer Paolo Bulgari Dead at 89

Paolo Bulgari—whose Bvlgari Group created unforgettable jewelry designs for stars like Elizabeth Taylor and Zendaya—has died at age 89.

Paolo Bulgari—famed jewelry designer and chairman of the Bvlgari Group—has died, the company confirmed on social media Nov. 21. He was 89.

“It is with deep sadness that we learned of the passing of Paolo Bulgari, grandson of the company’s founder Sotirio Bulgari and Chairman of the Bvlgari Group since 1984,” the company said in a statement shared to Instagram. “Our deepest condolences go to his family, friends and all those who had the honor of sharing this journey with him.”

“Thank you, Mr. Paolo,” they added, “your legacy as a brilliant beacon of creative inspiration will continue to inspire generations to come.”

Born in Rome, Italy, in 1937, Bulgari—who shared four kids with ex-wife Alice Valli as well as two kids with wife Maite Caprio—was destined to carry on the family business from a young age.

“Paolo Bulgari began collaborating with his father in 1960,” the statement explained, “specializing in the knowledge of precious stones, of which he was one of the world’s leading experts, and refining the sensibility and aesthetic sense that are at the root of the Bvlgari style.”

And it wasn’t long until he started making his own mark on the brand.

“A true creative soul, he poured his heart into his craft and into nurturing the talents of young designers,” added the statement, “leaving an indelible mark on the world of jewelry.”

In fact, Bulgari, alongside his brothers Gianni Bulgari and Nicola Bulgari, played an integral role in shaping the brand’s distinctive style, becoming known for their use of bold shapes and standout gems.

They also expanded the business from jewelry into watches, perfumes and even hotels.

And over the decades, the brand’s creations have adorned stars from Elizabeth Taylor and Princess Diana to Zendaya and Anne Hathaway.

Just last month, Kim Kardashian said she might just “faint” in a video shared to Instagram Oct. 28 while getting a private tour of Taylor’s jewelry collection at the Bvlgari store in Italy, in which she was able to try on one of the late actress’ beloved pieces—an emerald and diamond necklace gifted to her by Richard Burton in 1962.

As Kardashian put it, “I am freaking out!”

And she of course had to thank her stylist Law Roach for making the dream come true, calling him on the phone to thank him for the “best” birthday present ever.

And while it’s true that Bulgari’s influence on fashion has stood the test of time, that’s because he believed “everything can be a source of inspiration.”

As he used to say, per Bvlgari’s statement, “There are no rules in creativity. Never.”

#762. ATEEZ Earn Fourth No. 1 on Billboard 200 With ‘GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6’

Plus, U2 achieves its 14th top 10 with the debut of Carnaval de Luz.

ATEEZ earn their fourth No. 1 on the Billboard 200 albums chart as GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6 debuts atop the tally (dated Nov. 28). It’s the 10th top 10-charted project for the act, all of which have come since 2022. With the arrival, ATEEZ stand alone as the group with the most top 10s in the 2020s. Among all acts this decade, only YoungBoy Never Broke Again (15) and Taylor Swift (14) have more.

GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6 bows with 195,000 equivalent album units earned in the United States in the week ending Nov. 19, largely driven by pure album sales (191,000).

Also in the top 10, U2 collects its 14th top 10 as the band’s new studio album, Carnaval de Luz, debuts at No. 4.

The Billboard 200 chart ranks the most popular albums of the week in the U.S. based on multi-metric consumption as measured in equivalent album units, compiled by Luminate. Units comprise album sales, track equivalent albums (TEA) and streaming equivalent albums (SEA). Each unit equals one album sale, or 10 individual tracks sold from an album, or 2,500 ad-supported or 1,000 paid/subscription on-demand official audio and video streams generated by songs from an album. The new Nov. 28, 2026-dated chart will be posted in full on Billboard‘s website on Nov. 24. For all chart news, follow @billboard and @billboardcharts on both X, formerly known as Twitter, and Instagram.

Of GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6’s 195,000 first-week equivalent album units, album sales comprise 191,000 (it debuts at No. 1 on the Top Album Sales chart), SEA units comprise 4,000 (equaling 4.04 million on-demand official streams of the set’s songs) and TEA units comprise a negligible sum.

ATEEZ have logged their 10 top 10s on the Billboard 200 consecutively. The act claimed its first top 10 with the No. 3-peaking THE WORLD EP.1 : MOVEMENT in 2022. In total, with 10 top 10s in the 2020s, ATEEZ now solely have the most top 10s among groups this decade. The act was previously tied with Stray Kids (which got its ninth top 10 — and ninth No. 1 — in August with This & That).

GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6’s album sales were bolstered by its availability across 32 CD and vinyl variants (all containing collectible items such as photocards and posters, with some items randomized), including signed editions.

Olivia Rodrigo’s you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love falls to No. 2 on the latest Billboard 200 with 62,000 equivalent album units earned (down 1%). Morgan Wallen’s chart-topping I’m the Problem is a non-mover at No. 3 with a little more than 49,000 (up less than 1%).

U2 achieves its 14th top 10-charted album on the Billboard 200 as Carnaval de Luz debuts at No. 4 with 49,000 equivalent album units earned. Of that sum, album sales comprise 42,500 (it debuts at No. 2 on Top Album Sales), SEA units comprise 5,500 (equaling 5.77 million on-demand official streams of the set’s songs) and TEA units comprise 1,000.

U2 notched its first top 10 album on the Billboard 200 with the No. 1 The Joshua Tree in 1987 and was last in the top 10 with 2023’s Songs of Surrender (No. 5 debut and peak).

The new album’s first-week sales were aided by its availability across 18 physical variants (vinyl, CD, cassette and Blu-ray audio disc).

Carnaval de Luz was preceded by its lead single “Silencio,” which marked the group’s 45th entry on the Alternative Airplay chart earlier in November (tying Foo Fighters for the most in the chart’s history).

Two former No. 1s are next up on the Billboard 200, as Noah Kahan’s The Great Divide rises a spot to No. 5 (47,000 equivalent album units earned, up 8%) and Ella Langley’s Dandelion is pushed down 5-6 (45,000, up 2%). Kahan’s Stick Season is steady at No. 7 (36,000, up 2%) while SZA’s chart-topping SOS steps 9-8 (32,000, up 6%). Rounding out the top 10 are Olivia Dean’s The Art of Loving (down a spot to No. 9 with 32,000, down less than 1%) and Lil Baby’s FRESH (falling 2-10 with 31,000, down 47%).

Luminate, the independent data provider to the Billboard charts, completes a thorough review of all data submissions used in compiling the weekly chart rankings. Luminate reviews and authenticates data. In partnership with Billboard, data deemed suspicious or unverifiable is removed, using established criteria, before final chart calculations are made and published.

#761. 'World's best could've lost 4-0' - but should Man Utd have done more at Anfield?

Ngumoha stars as Liverpool thrash 10-man Man Utd

Mauricio Pochettino believes even the best team in the world could have conceded four goals at Liverpool in Manchester United's circumstances - but should the struggling Red Devils have done more in another disappointing defeat?

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager's first match in charge of United got off to a dreadful start as they had defender Leny Yoro sent off in the eighth minute and were 2-0 down by the 13th minute.

That left them with a mountain to climb, with Liverpool scoring twice more in the second half to secure a 4-0 win that kept United second from bottom in the table.

"Do you think that is easy?" said Pochettino of the situation that faced his new side after those woeful opening 13 minutes.

"Even the best team in the world playing like this in this situation, in our circumstance, maybe concede the four goals or maybe more. And now what we are going to say?

"We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing room."

Mauricio Pochettino post-match interview - Liverpool v Man Utd

Trying to win any game when reduced to 10 men in the first half is difficult. In the entire history of the Premier League Manchester United have managed it on four occasions - each of those at Old Trafford.

Indeed, in the 509 instances of a team receiving one or more red cards in the first half of a Premier League match, they have gone on to win just 88 times.

At Anfield it gets even more difficult, with Arsenal the only team to have beaten Liverpool on their own ground after a first-half dismissal.

For ex-Manchester United captain Roy Keane, though, there are ways to lose if you have a man sent off - and a 4-0 defeat was not one of them.

Speaking before Pochettino's comments, he told Sky Sports: "Are you telling me they couldn't have done better? They lose 4-0 and everyone is saying it's not too bad.

"Has a team ever got a result before with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality. I can't believe what I'm hearing from people who have played for the club saying 4-0 is not too bad."

Keane was responding to his former team-mate Gary Neville, who was part of the commentary team for Sky Sports.

"That's where we've got to, where we're starting to write off 4-0 defeats at Anfield as though it's just the norm and what should be accepted," said Neville in the closing stages of the game. "The club's standards have dropped so far it's incredible."

The former England full-back added: "There'll be an element of, 'let's just forget about this game because Yoro got sent off, we've got 10 men and all that sort of stuff', but it rides into the game in midweek and from a defensive perspective I've never seen anything like this."

Keane did not agree with that view as he said: "Liverpool should have scored eight or nine. Unbelievable chances they had and everyone's coming off the pitch saying four is not too bad.

"I feel like swearing. I'll try not to. How can anyone say 4-0 is not too bad? Just because they went down to 10 men. That obviously made it a lot more difficult, but if you go down to 10 men is that it? Do you down tools and throw the towel in?"

Chaotic week, nightmare start and huge reality check for Pochettino

Pochettino endures nightmare start as Man Utd lose to Liverpool

The red card that changed Liverpool-Man Utd: correct call?

Despite Keane's comments, a 4-0 loss at Anfield isn't unthinkable - certainly better than losing 7-0 as United did three years ago.

But in the wider context it provides more concern about a defence that is now officially the worst in Europe's top five leagues.

No other team in the Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Ligue 1 or Serie A has conceded more than United's 34 goals in all competitions so far this season.

It is also the second successive game they have conceded four goals, while in their last six games in all competitions they have conceded 19.

"I don't think Mauricio Pochettino can write this off," said ex-Leeds and Spurs goalkeeper Paul Robinson on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"He has to learn from it. He will have learned about his players and their attitude.

"Liverpool had 27 shots in that game. There were mitigating circumstances early in the game... but why did we get to those circumstances?

"It was because defenders were out of position again. The long ball over the top that catches Matthijs de Ligt out, the lack of communication, the tackle Leny Yoro makes and the defenders being caught out."

#760. A 'wow' player - why Ngumoha is already a Liverpool game-changer

Rio Ngumoha is going to be a 'wow' player for Liverpool - and he showed everyone exactly what he is already capable of in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United.

He made an outstanding assist then added a fine finish, and there is much more to come. He plays without fear so he is going to score and make many more goals the same way.

Ngumoha has only just turned 18 but he is already a game-changer, someone who gets people excited because he is so hard to stop when he is one-on-one.

Of course he can frustrate you at times too, but that's what creative and explosive wingers like him do - and it's because he is so talented that everyone wants to see an end product from him every time he gets on the ball.

There were times against United when Ngumoha did not quite deliver, but he is still so young and I would much rather see players like him take too many touches - or try too many things and fail - than be afraid to try them in the first place.

So, if he runs out of play or runs into too many players at times, because teams are doubling up on him like United were, that just shows how scared they are of him.

His ability means he occupies opposition players - Youri Tielemans was always backing up Diogo Dalot on his wing to try to help him out, but that just meant United were leaving someone else free.

Ngumoha stars as Liverpool thrash 10-man Man Utd

Sometimes it is actually harder when you are playing out wide against 10 men because you don't get the same amount of space - United were not attacking the same way they would have done with 11, and they were sitting in more.

Yes, Ngumoha ran up the odd blind alley or got outnumbered but that is always going to happen. As he learns, and gets even better, his decision-making will improve too. He will know when to try to go past people or when to find that free man instead.

But he still showed all the bravery you want from a winger against United and, when you keep trying things the way he did, something is going to come off for you.

I look at Bradley Barcola in a similar way to Ngumoha - he can be frustrating but he tries things, and can be brilliant.

For Liverpool right now, one of the biggest positives is the competition they have in wide areas, with those two plus Victor Munoz and Cody Gakpo.

There are other areas of their squad, like left-back or central midfield, where that competition needs to improve, but I don't really worry about the wide attacking areas in the same way.

Sunday was only Ngumoha's second Premier League start of the season, and his first since the opening day.

He maybe only got his chance because Gakpo has a calf problem but, when everyone is fit, it is really exciting that they will all be thinking they have to play their best to push the manager and get in the team.

Andoni Iraola post-match interview - Liverpool v Man Utd

There were plenty of other positives for Liverpool, too. All in all, Sunday could not have gone much better for them.

United made a woeful start with poor concentration and mistakes which cost them but, from there, Liverpool saw the game out well.

Just because the opposition has a man sent off early on does not mean any kind of victory is a given, let alone a 4-0 win.

Look at how United's 11 men lost to City's 10 in the Manchester derby earlier this season - we've seen many times how good teams can frustrate a side with an extra player like that.

It definitely does not mean you are going to steamroller them, but Liverpool did that and made an abundance of chances to get even more goals.

Days like this are so important for building belief in all their attacking players, especially because they were playing at home, and against their big rivals.

Up until now, it had felt like Liverpool's better days this season had come on the road, but now the pressure and expectation is off them a bit - particularly if, like Ngumoha or Florian Wirtz, you have scored and played well.

I know from experience that, the next time they go back to Anfield, they will be buzzing. You know that the fans are already with you after you've scored against United, and you feel the love a little bit more.

This is the start of a big week for Liverpool and Iraola will probably make changes against Club Brugge in Belgium on Wednesday, knowing how difficult Sunday's Merseyside derby will be.

Everton is always a tough game but I think Liverpool will enjoy their trip to Hill Dickinson Stadium, and the confidence they will have after beating United will mean they can go there with a really positive mindset.

Danny Murphy was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

#759. Quentin Tarantino and Wife Daniella Pick Welcome Baby No. 3

Quentin Tarantino and his wife Daniella Pick shared that they have welcomed their third baby together, a boy, with the new addition joining their kids Leo, 6, and Ariana, 4.

Once upon a time… Quentin Tarantino became a father of three.

Four years after the birth of their second child, the Oscar winner and his wife Daniella Pick Tarantino welcomed their third baby, Quentin’s rep confirmed to People Nov. 22.

“Quentin Tarantino and his wife, Daniella Pick Tarantino, are overjoyed to announce the birth of their third child,” the rep said in a statement to the outlet, “a baby boy.”

The couple—who tied the knot in 2018—also share son Leo, 6, and daughter Ariana, 4.

And while Quentin, 63, has kept his family life rather private, he has described fatherhood as an emotional experience.

“I can’t even see his name written on a piece of paper without crying,” the Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood filmmaker told CBS This Morning in July 2021, referring to Leo, whom he praised as the “most charming human being I’ve ever met in my life.”

“Half the time, I look at him and I’m just laughing because he’s so funny,” he continued. “And the other time, I’m just bursting into tears.”

And though Quentin’s first born shares a first name with one of his frequent collaborators Leonardo DiCaprio, he and his wife didn’t choose the moniker because of the Titanic star.

“We almost didn't name him [Leo] because people would assume that I named him after Leonardo DiCaprio,” Quentin shared during a June 2021 appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live. “There's nothing wrong with that but I didn't.”

“He's named after my wife's grandfather,” Quentin said, “but also because, just in our hearts, he was our little lion.”

And for the Pulp Fiction director—who splits his time between Los Angeles and his wife’s native Tel Avi, Israel—fatherhood has been his top priority.

After all, Quentin revealed last year that he was delaying his tenth and final film to focus on his family.

“The idea of jumping on a voyage when they’re too young to understand it is not enticing to me," the Hateful Eight filmmaker said of his kids at the 2025 Sundance Film Festival, per People. “I want to not do whatever movie I end up doing until my son is at least 6. That way he’ll know what’s going on, he’ll be there, and it will be a memory for the rest of his life.”
